enrichment.summary: Add Record Relation: links a target record onto a named relation field of an owner record in the cloud database.
enrichment.description: Add Record Relation writes a relation — a typed link between database records — rather than a property value: when `store` fires, the record identified by `targetId` is added to the configured relation field of the record identified by `modelId`. `relationAdded` confirms; `failure`/`error` report rejection (missing ids, access control). The reverse operation is Remove Record Relation with identical wiring.
enrichment.whenToUse: Many-to-many and one-to-many links the schema models as relations: project members, favourites, tags. For plain foreign-key style references stored as a string property, Set Record Properties on an id property is simpler.

ports.modelId: Id of the owner record (the one whose relation field gains a link).
ports.targetId: Id of the record being linked.
ports.store: Signal; performs the write against the cloud database.
ports.relationAdded: Signal; the server confirmed the link.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: The class and relation-name choices come from the project's database schema (declared-port-groups + runtime-discovered): the editor generates the pickers and any per-class ports from the schema, so the port set depends on the configured backend, not the node type.
patterns: Ids arrive over wires (component inputs, query outputs); the relation nodes only act on them.

dynamicPorts.description: Accepts an unbounded numbered series of inputs (see numberedInputs); ports are named "<base> <N>" counting from 0.

parameterEncoding.reason: The port helper needs project context this generator cannot supply headlessly — a live component, a connected node, or a backend schema.

enrichment.summary: Logical AND over any number of boolean inputs: Result is true only while every connected input is true.
enrichment.description: And combines an unbounded series of boolean inputs into one boolean `result` (Result) value output. The result is true only when at least one input is connected and none of them is false — inputs are coerced with plain JavaScript truthiness, so an input that has never received a value counts as false. Whenever any input changes, the result is recomputed and pushed downstream. This is a pure value node: it has no signals and no memory beyond its inputs' latest values.
enrichment.whenToUse: Use it to require several conditions at once — e.g. two checkboxes both ticked before enabling a button. For 'any of' semantics use Or; for a single negation use Inverter; for arithmetic or comparisons that produce the booleans in the first place, use Expression, then combine here (or fold the whole thing into one Expression if it reads better).

ports.result: Boolean value; true only while every connected input is true. With no inputs connected it is false.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: Inputs are numbered ports named "input 0", "input 1", … counting from 0 (displayed as "Input 0", "Input 1"). The editor always offers one more port than is currently connected, so connecting to the highest port makes the next one appear. An authoring tool should connect booleans to "input N" names, using consecutive indices starting at 0.
patterns: Several `checked` outputs → "input 0", "input 1", … with `result` → a button's `enabled`: require every consent before proceeding.
`result` → a Condition's `condition` when you need signal outputs (fired on evaluation) instead of a level.

ssr.note: The scheduler clock is frozen during server render; animations do not run or complete there.

It is deprecated and hidden from the node picker; States covers state-shaped animation and Animate To Value covers single-value tweens.

inputs.name: treatEmptyAs
inputs.description: Back-compat for graphs written before Variables were nullable. `null` (default) keeps a cleared value distinguishable from a real false. Choosing another option restores the pre-NDA-003 coercion for authors who relied on it.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The empty-value contract (dev-docs/reference/EMPTY-VALUE-CONTRACT.md): `undefined` abstains and leaves the Variable's stored value untouched. `null` is a real value — it clears the Variable, is stored, and fires Changed. What "cleared" is stored as is controlled by `Treat empty as` (null by default).

outputs.name: savedValue
outputs.description: Can be `null` — a cleared Variable (see `value`'s description) stores and emits null by default, not this type's zero value, unless `Treat empty as` says otherwise.

enrichment.summary: Per-instance true/false holder: stores one boolean locally, optionally latching new values until a Set signal fires.
enrichment.description: Boolean holds a single true/false value that belongs to this node instance alone — it is not named or shared (for an app-wide named value use Variable2). The `value` input sets it and `savedValue` (Value) reads it back. While the `saveValue` (Set) signal input is unconnected, values written to `value` apply immediately; once `saveValue` is connected the node latches: incoming values are held pending and only applied when Set fires. Incoming values are cast with JavaScript Boolean(). `changed` fires only when the stored value actually changes; `stored` fires after every Set trigger, changed or not.
enrichment.whenToUse: Use it for a local flag inside one component — 'has clicked', 'panel expanded' — especially the latch shape (pin `value` to true, fire Set from a signal) that turns a momentary signal into a level. For state shared across components use Variable2 + Set Variable; for multi-state logic use States.

ports.value: Boolean value input. Applies immediately when `saveValue` is unconnected; otherwise held until Set fires.
ports.saveValue: Signal; applies the most recently received `value`, then fires `stored`. Connecting it switches the node from pass-through to latch mode.
ports.savedValue: Boolean level with the currently stored value; wire to inputs like `visible` or `enabled`.
ports.changed: Signal; fires only when the stored value actually changes, not on every Set.
ports.stored: Signal; fires after every Set trigger, even when the value did not change.

patterns: Latch a signal into a level: set `value` to true in parameters, wire the signal to `saveValue`, and read `savedValue` — a sticky 'this has happened' flag.
`savedValue` → Condition `condition` to branch signal flow on the stored flag.
antiPatterns: Using two Boolean nodes in different components to 'share' a flag — each instance has its own value and they never sync. Use Variable2 for shared state.

enrichment.summary: Picks between two strings based on a boolean: outputs String for true or String for false.
enrichment.description: Boolean To String selects one of two configured strings using the boolean `input` (Selector): while the selector is true, `currentValue` (Current Value) is `trueString` (String for true); otherwise it is `falseString` (String for false). The output updates whenever the selector or the currently selected string changes, and `inputChanged` (Selector Changed) fires as a signal each time the selector itself flips. Both strings are usually set as parameters but can also be connected.
enrichment.whenToUse: Use it to turn app state into UI copy: a toggle button's label, an on/off status caption, a yes/no cell. For mapping more than two cases, use String Mapper (string keys) or States; for text with variable parts inside it, use String Format.

ports.input: Boolean value (displayed as Selector) that chooses which string appears on the output.
ports.currentValue: String value: `trueString` while the selector is true, `falseString` otherwise.
ports.inputChanged: Signal; fires when the selector changes value — not when the strings themselves are edited.

patterns: Switch `state` → `input`, `currentValue` → the same toggle button's `label`: the button always names the action it will perform next.

enrichment.summary: An SVG circle or arc with fill, stroke and start/end angles — the quick way to dots, rings and progress arcs.
enrichment.description: Circle draws a circular shape as inline SVG. `size` is the diameter in pixels; `fillEnabled`/`fillColor` and `strokeEnabled`/`strokeColor`/`strokeWidth` control the two paint layers independently. `startAngle` and `endAngle` (degrees, measured clockwise from 12 o'clock, defaults 0–360) cut the shape into an arc: a partial angle range with fill gives a pie slice, with stroke only it gives an arc — driving `endAngle` from a number is the standard way to build a progress ring. It cannot have children; like other visual nodes it reports `onClick`, hover and pointer signals.
enrichment.whenToUse: Status dots, avatars' presence badges, decorative shapes, and progress rings/pie indicators. For rectangular surfaces or anything that needs children use Group (with corner radius for rounded shapes); for pictures use Image; for glyphs use net.noodl.visual.icon.

ports.size: Number value; the circle's diameter in pixels (default 100).
ports.startAngle: Number value in degrees, 0 at the top and increasing clockwise; together with `endAngle` restricts the shape to an arc.
ports.endAngle: Number value in degrees (default 360). Animate or bind 0–360 here for a progress ring.
ports.strokeLineCap: Enum 'butt' or 'round'; 'round' gives arcs soft ends, visible on partial angle ranges.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: Declared-port-groups: the only conditional port is `pointerEventsEnabled`, which appears when `pointerEventsMode` is set to 'explicit'. Everything else in the catalog's port list is always present.
patterns: Progress ring: stroke enabled, fill disabled, a 0–100 value remapped to 0–360 (Number Remapper or Expression) driving `endAngle`.
Status dot: small `size`, `fillColor` bound from state — cheaper than an image asset.

It is deprecated and hidden from the node picker; CloudFunction2 supersedes it, targeting a cloud function component built with `noodl.cloud.request`/`noodl.cloud.response` and mirroring that component's declared parameters and results as typed ports instead of a free-form name and result blob.

enrichment.summary: Calls a cloud function component from the browser: send parameters, run the server-side graph, receive its results.
enrichment.description: Cloud Function is the browser-side caller of a cloud function — a component that lives on the cloud runtime and starts with a Request node and ends with a Response node. Pick the target in the `function` input; the node then grows one `in-<name>` input per parameter declared on the function's Request node and one `out-<name>` output per value declared on its Response nodes. Triggering `call` (Call, signal) POSTs the current `in-` values to the server, where the function's graph runs; when the Response sends a success reply the `out-` outputs update and `success` (signal) fires. On a failure reply — or any transport error — `error` (string value) is set and `failure` (signal) fires. The logged-in user's session token is sent along automatically, so the function sees the caller's identity.
enrichment.whenToUse: Use it whenever browser logic needs work done with server-side trust: secrets, security-sensitive writes, aggregations, or multi-record transactions. For plain reads of database classes prefer DbCollection2 (Query Records) directly. Do not use the deprecated v1 'Cloud Function' node in new graphs.

ports.call: Signal input; sends the request with the current `in-` parameter values after all pending input updates have been applied.
ports.success: Signal; fires after a success response, after all `out-` outputs have been updated with the returned results.
ports.failure: Signal; fires when the function replies with failure status or the request itself fails. Read `error` for the message.
ports.error: String value with the last error message (the Response node's Error Message on a failure reply).

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: Ports are mirrored from the targeted cloud function component by the editor's CloudFunctionAdapter. The `function` input (edit-only) lists every component that contains a `noodl.cloud.request` node — cloud function components live under the `/#__cloud__/` sheet, and the parameter stores the component name without that prefix. Each name in the Request node's `params` list becomes an `in-<name>` input; each name in the Response nodes' `params` lists becomes an `out-<name>` output. All are type '*'; an authoring tool must read the target component's Request/Response `params` to know which ports exist.
patterns: Button `onClick` → `call`, `out-<name>` → visual inputs: the request/response cycle for an action the client must not perform itself.
`success` → a Query Records fetch action: refresh client data after a server-side write.
antiPatterns: Wiring `out-` outputs somewhere without also handling `failure` leaves errors invisible — surface `error` in the UI or react to `failure`.

enrichment.summary: Deprecated all-in-one shared array node. Use Collection2 (Array) plus the CollectionInsert/Remove/Clear/New action nodes.
enrichment.description: The legacy Collection node bundled the shared-list store and all its mutations (add/remove/clear/new/store/fetch) into one node. Its replacement splits reading (Array/Collection2) from the individual mutation nodes, keeping graphs legible. The underlying shared-by-id array store is the same, so legacy and current nodes interoperate on the same `collectionId`s.
enrichment.whenToUse: Do not use in new graphs — use Collection2 with CollectionInsert/CollectionRemove/CollectionClear/CollectionNew instead.

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: undefined leaves this Array's current collection alone (no opinion supplied). null clears it — every item is removed and Changed fires once, the same as connecting an empty collection.

enrichment.summary: Array: binds to a shared client-side array by id — read its items and count, seed its contents, and react to changes made anywhere.
enrichment.description: Client-side arrays live in a global registry keyed by id: every node that names the same id — this node, Insert/Remove/Clear Array nodes, other components — reads and mutates the same underlying array. Collection2 binds to the array named on `collectionId` (Id) and exposes it on `items` (the live array), plus `count`, `firstItemId` and `id`. Whenever the array's contents change — from any node or code, anywhere in the app — `changed` fires and `count`/`firstItemId` update. Connecting an array to the `items` input copies that source array's contents into this array, and keeps re-copying while the source changes. If `fetch` (signal) is connected the node defers: a new `collectionId` only takes effect when `fetch` fires (then `fetched` fires), and automatic `changed` events are suppressed.
enrichment.whenToUse: Local list state shared across components without any wiring between them: give every interested node the same Array Id. For server data use DbCollection2 (Query Records); for a single object use Model2 (Object); to mutate the array use Insert/Remove/Clear Array nodes rather than manipulating `items` in code.

ports.collectionId: Value input: the shared array's id. Every node using the same id operates on the same array.
ports.items: As input (value): copies the connected source array's contents into this array, tracking later source changes. As output (value): the shared array itself — feed a Repeater's `items`.
ports.fetch: Signal input; when connected, id changes are deferred until this fires, and the automatic `changed` output is suppressed — use for explicit control over when the node (re)binds.
ports.changed: Signal; fires after the array's contents change from anywhere in the app (suppressed while `fetch` is connected).
ports.fetched: Signal; fires after an explicit `fetch` has re-bound the array.
ports.firstItemId: String value: the id of the array's first object, or empty when the array is empty.

patterns: Same `collectionId` in many components: a list page shows the array while a form elsewhere inserts into it — no connections needed between them.
`items` → For Each `items`: the canonical local list.
Feed `collectionId` from Create New Array `id` to bind to a dynamically created array.
antiPatterns: Using it for cloud data — it is purely client-side, nothing is persisted; use DbCollection2 (Query Records) instead.

enrichment.summary: Clear Array: empties a shared array (removes all items) when Do fires.
enrichment.description: When `clear` (Do) fires, resolves `collectionId` (Array Id) to the shared array, replaces its contents with an empty list, and fires `modified` (Done). The Array Id must be set before the signal arrives. The objects that were in the array are not destroyed — only the array is emptied — and every node bound to the same Array Id sees the empty array immediately.
enrichment.whenToUse: Reset-style actions on local shared arrays ('clear the list', 'empty the cart'). To remove a single item use Remove Object From Array; this node is all-or-nothing.

ports.clear: Signal input (Do); empties the array. Requires `collectionId` to be set.
ports.collectionId: Value input: id of the shared array to empty.
ports.modified: Signal (Done); fires after the array has been emptied.

enrichment.summary: Insert Object Into Array: appends an existing object, referenced by its id, to a shared array when Do fires.
enrichment.description: When `add` (Do) fires, resolves `collectionId` (Array Id) to the shared array and `modifyId` (Object Id) to the shared object, appends the object to the end of the array, and fires `modified` (Done). Both ids must be set — a missing Object Id or Array Id raises an editor warning and nothing happens. Because arrays are shared by id, every Array node and Repeater bound to the same Array Id sees the new item immediately.
enrichment.whenToUse: Adding items to a local shared array — typically right after Create New Object has created the object to add. For removing use Remove Object From Array; for cloud data use the record nodes instead (nothing here is persisted).

ports.add: Signal input (Do); performs the insert after other inputs have settled.
ports.collectionId: Value input: id of the shared array to append to.
ports.modifyId: Connection-only value input: the id of the object to insert — typically Create New Object's `id` output.
ports.modified: Signal (Done); fires after the object has been appended.

patterns: Create New Object `created` → `add` and `id` → `modifyId`: the canonical create-then-insert flow.
antiPatterns: Trying to insert a raw value or JS object — `modifyId` takes an object id, not the data itself; create an object first with Create New Object.

enrichment.summary: Create New Array: makes a fresh array with a generated id when Do fires, optionally copying an input array's contents into it.
enrichment.description: On the `new` (Do) signal, creates a brand-new shared array under a freshly generated unique id. If an array is connected to `items`, its current contents are copied into the new array once, at creation time — later changes to the source are not tracked, so the result is a snapshot. After creation, `id` outputs the new array's id and `created` (Done) fires. Each trigger of Do creates another new array.
enrichment.whenToUse: When you need an anonymous or per-instance array instead of one fixed well-known id — e.g. snapshotting a live array before batch-processing it, or creating a sub-array whose id you store on an object. If one well-known shared array is enough, just use Array (Collection2) with a fixed id.

ports.new: Signal input (Do); creates the array. Every trigger creates a new array with a new id.
ports.items: Value input; the contents to copy into the new array at creation time. A one-time snapshot, not a live link.
ports.id: String value: the generated id of the most recently created array. Feed it to an Array node's `collectionId` or an Insert/Remove node's Array Id.
ports.created: Signal (Done); fires after the array exists and `id` is valid.

patterns: `id` → Collection2 `collectionId`: bind an Array node to the newly created array to read it.
Snapshot before a batch: source `items` → this `items`, Do on the user action, `created` → Run Tasks `run`.

enrichment.summary: Remove Object From Array: removes an object, referenced by its id, from a shared array when Do fires.
enrichment.description: When `remove` (Do) fires, resolves `collectionId` (Array Id) to the shared array and `modifyId` (Object Id) to the shared object, removes that object from the array, and fires `modified` (Done). If either id is unset, nothing happens. Only the array membership changes — the object itself continues to exist and can still be reached by its id. Every Array node and Repeater bound to the same Array Id updates immediately.
enrichment.whenToUse: Per-item delete actions in local lists. Inside a Repeater's item component, feed `modifyId` from Repeater Item's `itemId` — that is the idiomatic 'remove this row'. For clearing everything use Clear Array; for cloud records use Delete Record.

ports.remove: Signal input (Do); performs the removal after other inputs have settled.
ports.collectionId: Value input: id of the shared array to remove from.
ports.modifyId: Connection-only value input: the id of the object to remove — inside a repeater item, wire Repeater Item `itemId` here.
ports.modified: Signal (Done); fires after the object has been removed.

patterns: Repeater Item `itemId` → `modifyId`, delete button `onClick` → `remove`, with the list's Array Id on `collectionId`: a per-row delete button.

inputs.name: treatEmptyAs
inputs.description: Back-compat for graphs written before Variables were nullable. `null` (default) keeps a cleared value distinguishable from a real "". Choosing another option restores the pre-NDA-003 coercion for authors who relied on it.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The empty-value contract (dev-docs/reference/EMPTY-VALUE-CONTRACT.md): `undefined` abstains and leaves the Variable's stored value untouched. `null` is a real value — it clears the Variable, is stored, and fires Changed. What "cleared" is stored as is controlled by `Treat empty as` (null by default).

outputs.name: savedValue
outputs.description: Can be `null` — a cleared Variable (see `value`'s description) stores and emits null by default, not this type's zero value, unless `Treat empty as` says otherwise.

enrichment.summary: Per-instance color holder: stores one color locally so many visual inputs can share a single editable source.
enrichment.description: Color holds a single color value that belongs to this node instance alone, defaulting to '#f1f2f4'. The `value` input sets it (via the editor's color picker or a connection) and `savedValue` (Value) reads it back. While the `saveValue` (Set) signal input is unconnected, values written to `value` apply immediately; once `saveValue` is connected the node latches: incoming values are held pending and only applied when Set fires. Unlike the Boolean/Number/String holders it applies no cast — the value passes through unchanged. Browser-only; not available in cloud functions. `changed` fires only when the stored value actually changes; `stored` fires after every Set trigger.
enrichment.whenToUse: Use it as a single source of truth for a color used in several places — wire `savedValue` to every `backgroundColor`, `color` or border input that should match, and edit one node to restyle them all. For project-wide theming prefer style colors; a String can also drive color inputs (any CSS color string casts), but Color gives you the picker.

ports.value: Color value input with the editor's color picker. Applies immediately when `saveValue` is unconnected; otherwise held until Set fires.
ports.saveValue: Signal; applies the most recently received `value`, then fires `stored`.
ports.savedValue: Color level with the currently stored color; fan it out to any number of visual color inputs.
ports.changed: Signal; fires only when the stored value actually changes.
ports.stored: Signal; fires after every Set trigger, even when the value did not change.

patterns: One accent color: `savedValue` → several nodes' `backgroundColor`/`color` inputs, so a design tweak is one edit.
Runtime theme switch: a Switch or States feeds `value`, and every connected visual updates together.

inputs.name: blendValue
inputs.description: Position along the colour list, where 1 is exactly Color 1 and 1.5 is halfway to Color 2; values outside the list are clamped

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: The blended colour as a hex string; the inputs must be 6-digit hex, since any other notation yields nonsense

dynamicPorts.description: Accepts an unbounded numbered series of inputs (see numberedInputs); ports are named "<base> <N>" counting from 0.

parameterEncoding.reason: The port helper needs project context this generator cannot supply headlessly — a live component, a connected node, or a backend schema.

enrichment.summary: Interpolates between configured colors as blendValue moves 0→1, outputting the mixed color.
enrichment.description: Color Blend holds a list of colors (`color-0`, `color-1`, … per its `colors` count) and outputs on `result` the interpolation selected by `blendValue`: 0 is the first color, 1 the last, values between blend smoothly across the sequence. Feed `blendValue` from an animated source and the color animates.
enrichment.whenToUse: Any color that should respond continuously to a value: hover highlights, scroll-linked tints, state colors with smooth transitions. For discrete color switches with no blending, States values are simpler.

ports.blendValue: Number 0–1 selecting the position along the color sequence.
ports.result: The interpolated color; wire to any color input (backgroundColor, fillColor, text color).

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: Numbered inputs: the `colors` count parameter generates `color-N` inputs (numbered-inputs mechanism); only `blendValue` is static.
patterns: Animate To Value `currentValue` → `blendValue` → a background color: the corpus's standard smooth-hover wiring (Color Blend → color inputs appears 21× in real projects).

nodes.shortDesc: Placeholder marking where children given to an instance of this component are inserted.

enrichment.summary: Placeholder inside a component's visual tree marking where children given to an instance of that component are inserted.
enrichment.description: Component Children is how a component becomes a wrapper. Placed somewhere in the component's own visual tree (typically inside a Group), it marks the insertion point: when a parent graph adds visual children to an *instance* of the component, those children render at exactly this position, surrounded by whatever chrome the component defines. The node has no inputs or outputs and renders nothing by itself — it is purely a structural marker. A component that contains one accepts children in the node picker; a component without one does not. A component has a single insertion point: adding more than one Component Children does not create multiple slots.
enrichment.whenToUse: Whenever you build a reusable container whose content varies per use — cards, page sections, modals, styled panels: define padding, borders, headers once in the wrapper component and drop Component Children where the caller's content goes. Not for repeating data-driven content (use For Each with a template component) and not for passing values into a component (use Component Inputs).
patterns: Wrapper component: Group root with the shared styling, a Text header bound from Component Inputs, and Component Children below it — instances then supply arbitrary content children.
Combine with Component Inputs: chrome configuration (title, variant) flows through inputs while free-form content flows through children.
antiPatterns: Placing several Component Children to try to create multiple named slots — only one insertion point exists per component; split into smaller wrapper components instead.

dynamicPorts.description: Output ports mirror the port names listed in this node's "ports" parameter; each becomes an input of the containing component and an output of this node.

parameterEncoding.reason: Ports mirror the component input declarations the author makes on this node; the names are whatever they typed, with no prefix or transformation.

enrichment.summary: Declares the component's own input ports; what the parent wires into an instance arrives on this node's outputs.
enrichment.description: Component Inputs defines the receiving half of a component's port surface. Every port added on this node becomes an input of the component itself: a parent graph wires values or signals into the component instance, and they emerge inside the component as this node's outputs. Inside a Repeater item component the same mechanism delivers item data — each property of the item object feeds the identically-named Component Input.
enrichment.whenToUse: Whenever a component needs data or triggers from its parent: item templates, reusable controls, page components. Use events (Send/Receive Event) only when sender and receiver are unrelated; parent→child always goes through Component Inputs.
enrichment.runtimeBehavior: All ports are author-declared on the node instance (component-ports mechanism): the catalog lists none because each component defines its own. The instance's ports also define the component's external inputs — tools should read them from the node instance's `ports`, never from the catalog.
patterns: Repeater item: declare inputs named after the item object's properties and bind them straight to visuals.
Signal inputs ('Show', 'Reset') let a parent drive behaviour without exposing internals.
antiPatterns: Reaching for global Variables to pass parent data into a child; that hides the dependency the port surface would document.

dynamicPorts.description: Input ports mirror the port names listed in this node's "ports" parameter; each becomes an output of the containing component and an input of this node.

parameterEncoding.reason: Ports mirror the component output declarations the author makes on this node; the names are whatever they typed, with no prefix or transformation.

enrichment.summary: Declares the component's own output ports; what the graph wires into this node is exposed on the component's instances.
enrichment.description: Component Outputs is the sending half of a component's port surface: every port added here becomes an output of the component itself, readable (values) or receivable (signals) wherever an instance of the component is placed. A Repeater additionally surfaces item components' output signals as ports on itself, so list events bubble up without extra plumbing.
enrichment.whenToUse: Expose results and events to the parent: a form component's 'Submitted' signal, a card's 'Selected' with the wired value, a wizard's completion. If several unrelated components must react, send an event instead.
enrichment.runtimeBehavior: All ports are author-declared on the node instance (component-ports mechanism); the catalog lists none. The instance's ports define the component's external outputs — read them from the node instance, never the catalog.
patterns: Worker/task components report 'success'/'failure' signals through Component Outputs; Run Tasks consumes exactly that surface.

dynamicPorts.description: Some ports are discovered at runtime from user code, parameters or connected components, and are pushed to the editor per instance; the static port list below is incomplete for such instances.

variables.property: one of the comma-separated entries in the `properties` parameter
one of the comma-separated entries in the `properties` parameter

enrichment.summary: Deprecated per-component-instance state store. Use Component Object (net.noodl.ComponentObject).
enrichment.description: The legacy Component State node held named values scoped to the component instance — the role now filled by Component Object, which shares the same instance-scoped store semantics with a clearer read/write split. Deprecated and hidden from the picker.
enrichment.whenToUse: Do not use in new graphs — use net.noodl.ComponentObject (with Set Component Object Properties) instead.
enrichment.runtimeBehavior: Property ports are generated from the per-instance `properties` list (runtime-discovered).

inputs.name: condition
inputs.description: Value to test for truth; it is re-tested on every change unless Evaluate is connected

inputs.name: eval
inputs.description: Tests Condition now; connecting this stops the node testing on every change, so nothing happens until it fires

outputs.name: isfalse
outputs.description: The opposite of Is True, so a false branch needs no Inverter

outputs.name: onfalse
outputs.description: Fires each time Condition is tested and found false, including while Condition has never been set

outputs.name: ontrue
outputs.description: Fires each time Condition is tested and found true — exactly one of On True and On False fires per test

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: Whether the last test found Condition true, for wiring into a value rather than branching on a signal

enrichment.summary: Boolean gate: routes an evaluation into On True / On False signals and holds Is True / Is False as readable booleans.
enrichment.description: Condition watches a single boolean input and exposes it in two forms: as level outputs (`result`/Is True and `isfalse`/Is False, plain booleans that always reflect the current state) and as event outputs (`ontrue`/On True and `onfalse`/On False, signals that fire when the condition is evaluated). Evaluation happens when the `condition` input changes, or on demand when the `eval` (Evaluate) signal is triggered — the idiomatic way to gate an action behind a check at the moment a user acts.
enrichment.whenToUse: Use it to branch signal flow ('when clicked, proceed only if valid') or to derive a visible/enabled boolean and its inverse from one condition. For choosing between more than two cases use Switch or States; for combining several booleans first, feed it from And/Or or an Expression.

ports.condition: Boolean value input. Changing it re-evaluates and fires the matching signal output.
ports.eval: Signal input; re-evaluates the current `condition` on demand and fires `ontrue` or `onfalse` accordingly. Wire a user action here to use Condition as a gate.
ports.ontrue: Signal; fires on evaluation while the condition is true — not a level, it will not re-fire until evaluated again.
ports.onfalse: Signal; fires on evaluation while the condition is false.
ports.result: Boolean level mirroring the condition; wire to inputs like `visible` or `enabled`.
ports.isfalse: Boolean level, inverse of `result`; saves an Inverter when driving 'error shown' style inputs.

patterns: Button `onClick` → `eval`, with `ontrue` driving the action: gate an action behind a validity check at click time.
`isfalse` → a message's `visible`: show an error as a level rather than pulsing it with a signal.
antiPatterns: Wiring `ontrue` (signal) to a boolean input like `visible` delivers only a momentary pulse — use `result` for anything that must stay on.

inputs.name: decrease
inputs.description: Subtracts one from the count, or does nothing at all when Limits Enabled and the count is already at Min Value

inputs.name: increase
inputs.description: Adds one to the count, or does nothing at all when Limits Enabled and the count is already at Max Value

inputs.name: limitsEnabled
inputs.description: Whether Min Value and Max Value bound the count; without it the count runs unbounded in both directions

inputs.name: limitsMax
inputs.description: Highest count Increase will reach, ignored unless Limits Enabled

inputs.name: limitsMin
inputs.description: Lowest count Decrease will reach, ignored unless Limits Enabled

inputs.name: reset
inputs.description: Puts the count back to Start Value

inputs.name: startValue
inputs.description: Count to begin at and to return to on Reset; setting it announces a change on Count Changed at page load

outputs.name: countChanged
outputs.description: Fires after the count has moved, and also once at page load when Start Value is set

outputs.name: currentCount
outputs.description: The count as it stands

enrichment.summary: A number you step up and down with signals, with optional min/max limits and a reset.
enrichment.description: Counter holds a number, exposed on `currentCount` (Current Count). The `increase` (Increase Count) and `decrease` (Decrease Count) signal inputs step it by exactly 1; `reset` (Reset To Start) puts it back to `startValue` (Start Value, default 0), which is also the initial count. When `limitsEnabled` (Limits Enabled) is true, an `increase` at or above `limitsMax` (Max Value) and a `decrease` at or below `limitsMin` (Min Value) are ignored entirely — the count does not change and `countChanged` does not fire. Every actual change fires the `countChanged` (Count Changed) signal after `currentCount` has been updated.
enrichment.whenToUse: Use it for user-driven tallies: quantity steppers, pagination cursors, wizard step tracking. For arbitrary arithmetic (step sizes other than 1, computed values) use Expression or a Function; for a persistent number shared across components use a Variable or an Object.

ports.increase: Signal; adds 1. Ignored (no change, no `countChanged`) when limits are enabled and the count is already at `limitsMax`.
ports.decrease: Signal; subtracts 1. Ignored when limits are enabled and the count is already at `limitsMin`.
ports.reset: Signal; sets the count back to `startValue` and fires `countChanged`.
ports.startValue: Number value; the initial count, and the value `reset` returns to. The first time it is set it also overwrites the current count.
ports.limitsEnabled: Boolean value (default false); turns `limitsMin`/`limitsMax` enforcement on. Enabling it does not clamp an already out-of-range count — it only blocks further steps past a limit.
ports.countChanged: Signal; fires once per actual change, after `currentCount` holds the new value.

patterns: Plus/minus buttons' `onClick` → `increase`/`decrease` with limits enabled: a bounded quantity stepper.
`currentCount` → a String Format input: display the count inside a sentence without a Function node.
antiPatterns: Polling `currentCount` to react to changes — wire `countChanged` (signal) or `currentCount` (value) directly; the node already pushes updates.

enrichment.summary: Formats a date into a string using {year}/{month}/{date}/{hours}-style tokens.
enrichment.description: Date To String takes a date on `input` (Date) — a Date object, or a date string which it converts with `new Date()` — and writes a formatted string to `currentValue` (Date String) according to `formatString` (Format). Supported tokens: {date} (day of month, 2-digit), {month} (2-digit), {monthShort} (e.g. "Jan", en-US), {year} (4-digit), {yearShort} (2-digit), {hours}, {minutes}, {seconds} (all 2-digit, 24-hour); anything else in the format passes through literally. The default format is "{year}-{month}-{date}". Each time formatting runs, `inputChanged` (Date Changed) fires; if the input is not a usable date, `currentValue` becomes an empty string and `onError` (Invalid Date) fires instead of throwing.
enrichment.whenToUse: Use it to display timestamps — record creation dates, 'last saved' times — without writing code. For formats beyond these tokens (locale-aware dates, relative times like '2 h ago'), use a Function node with Intl or a date library. Note there is no {day}-of-week token.

ports.input: Date value input; also accepts a date string, converted with new Date(). An unparsable value routes to `onError`.
ports.formatString: String value with the tokens above; changing it reformats the current date immediately.
ports.currentValue: String value with the formatted result; empty string after a formatting error.
ports.inputChanged: Signal; fires each time formatting runs (new date, and reformat after a format change).
ports.onError: Signal; fires when formatting fails (e.g. invalid date), in which case `currentValue` is emptied.

patterns: A Function output producing `new Date()` on demand → `input`: timestamp an event, then show `currentValue` in a String Format sentence.
antiPatterns: Wiring a number (epoch milliseconds) to `input` — number does not cast to date; convert to a Date in a Function or Expression first.

enrichment.summary: Query Records: fetches records of a cloud database class with filter/sort/limit, keeps results live, and outputs them as an array.
enrichment.description: Query Records reads a class from the connected cloud database and exposes the matching records on `items` (an array of record objects), with `count`, `firstItemId` and `isEmpty` alongside. The query — class name, visual or JavaScript filter, sorting, limit and pagination — is configured in the node's parameters. Results are live by default: when a record elsewhere in the app is created, saved or deleted, the node re-checks it against the current query and updates `items` in place. `fetched` fires when a fetch completes, `failure`/`error` report problems.
enrichment.whenToUse: The starting point of every cloud-data list or lookup in browser logic. For writing data use Create/Save/Delete New Record nodes; for a single record by id use Model2/DbModel2; in cloud functions querying is available too (availableIn: cloud).

ports.items: Array output with the query result; the canonical source for a Repeater's `items`.
ports.fetched: Signal; fires each time a fetch (initial or re-run) completes.
ports.isEmpty: Boolean level; drive empty-state visuals from here rather than comparing `count` yourself.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: All *inputs* are runtime-determined (runtime-discovered + editor-adapter): the class choice, filter values, sort keys and paging inputs are generated from the project's database schema and the visual filter you build in the editor — e.g. each 'value' placeholder in a filter becomes its own input port, and actions like fetch ('storageFetch') are registered on demand. A generator cannot enumerate them statically; an authoring tool should set `collectionName` and filter parameters, and may wire signals to fetch-related inputs which the runtime registers when used.
patterns: `items` → Repeater `items`, with record properties delivered to the item component via Component Inputs: the canonical list page.
Event Receiver `eventReceived` → fetch input: re-run a query on demand from anywhere in the app.
antiPatterns: Re-querying on a timer to feel 'live' — results already update from cloud events; explicit re-fetch is only needed when the server changed outside those events.

dynamicPorts.description: Some ports are discovered at runtime from user code, parameters or connected components, and are pushed to the editor per instance; the static port list below is incomplete for such instances.

parameterEncoding.reason: Ports follow the database configuration schema fetched from the backend.

enrichment.summary: Config: reads one named parameter from the cloud service's config and outputs its value.
enrichment.description: DbConfig (Config) fetches the cloud service's config once when the node initializes and outputs the value of the parameter chosen with the `configKey` (Parameter) input — server-managed settings like feature flags, welcome texts or API keys, edited on the cloud service rather than baked into the app. The `value` output is typed from the config schema (string, boolean, number, object or array). A Local Override group (`useDevValue` Enable + `devValue` Value) lets you substitute a local value, but only while running locally with the editor connected — deployed apps always read the real config.
enrichment.whenToUse: Use it whenever behaviour or copy should be changeable on the server without redeploying the app. It is read-only and fetched once at startup; for per-record data use DbCollection2 / DbModel2, and for values the app computes itself use Variable or Object nodes.

ports.value: Value output with the selected config parameter; typed from the config schema, updates once the config has loaded (and when a local override changes).

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: All ports are runtime-determined from the project's cloud config schema (`dbConfigSchema` metadata): `configKey` is registered as an edit-only enum of the parameter names (master-key-only parameters are listed only in cloud functions), the `value` output takes the selected parameter's type, and the Local Override inputs (`useDevValue`, then `devValue` when enabled) appear for basic types. An authoring tool should set `configKey` in parameters and read the `value` output; the editor warns if the key does not exist in the schema.
patterns: `value` → a Text's `text`: server-editable copy such as banners or announcement messages.
`value` (boolean parameter) → a Group's `visible` or a Button's `enabled`: feature flags without redeploying.

enrichment.summary: Deprecated cloud record node that mixed reading, writing and deleting in one node; superseded by DbModel2 and the dedicated write nodes.
enrichment.description: DbModel (Model) is the original cloud-record node: one node that fetched, created, saved and deleted a database record via `fetch`, `new`, `insert`, `save` and `delete` signal inputs. It is deprecated and hidden from the node picker. Reading a record is now done with DbModel2 (Record); writing is split into NewDbModelProperties (Create New Record), SetDbModelProperties (Set Record Properties) and DeleteDbModelProperties (Delete Record), which are simpler to reason about because each node performs exactly one operation.

enrichment.summary: Record: binds to one cloud database record by id and exposes each of its properties as an output that follows the record.
enrichment.description: DbModel2 (Record) points at a single record of a cloud database class and exposes one value output per property of that class (registered as `prop-<property>`), plus a `changed-<property>` signal per property. Setting `modelId` binds the node to the record in the app's local record store — properties already known locally (for example from a Query Records result) appear immediately, and `fetched` fires. Triggering `fetch` (Fetch, signal) loads the record fresh from the server by id; while `fetch` is connected, local change events no longer drive the outputs, so updates arrive only when you fetch. `changed` fires whenever the bound record changes from anywhere in the app (a Set Record Properties elsewhere, a live query update).
enrichment.whenToUse: Use it to read one record's properties — a detail page, or the current item inside a repeater (set `idSource` to 'From repeater'). It does not write: pair it with SetDbModelProperties to save edits. For lists of records use DbCollection2 (Query Records); for records from a non-cloud (BYOB) backend use noodl.byob.QueryData, whose results are plain objects, not records.

ports.modelId: Value input (connections only): the record id to bind to; a full record object is also accepted and dereferenced to its id.
ports.idSource: Edit-only choice: 'Specify explicitly' uses `modelId`; 'From repeater' binds to the record driving the nearest enclosing For Each item.
ports.fetch: Signal; fetches the record from the server by the current `modelId`. Connecting it also switches the node to fetch-driven mode: outputs update on Fetch instead of on local record changes.
ports.fetched: Signal; fires after the record resolves — on bind when `fetch` is not connected, or after a server fetch completes.
ports.changed: Signal; fires when the bound record's data changes anywhere in the app (suppressed while `fetch` is connected).
ports.id: String value; the id of the currently bound record.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: Property ports are runtime-determined from the cloud database class selected via the `collectionName` parameter (itself a runtime-registered enum of the project's classes plus _User and _Role): each schema property becomes a value output `prop-<name>` (typed from the schema) and a signal output `changed-<name>`. Relation properties get no ports. An authoring tool should set `collectionName` in parameters and may reference `prop-<name>`/`changed-<name>` for properties it knows exist in the class schema.
patterns: Component Inputs `<id>` → `modelId`, with `prop-<name>` outputs driving the page: the canonical detail-page shape where a list passes the record id to a detail component.
`prop-<name>` → a Text Input's `startValue`, edited text → Set Record Properties `prop-<name>`: prefill an edit form and save it back.
antiPatterns: Connecting `fetch` just to 'refresh' — while `fetch` is connected the node stops following local record changes, so only do it when you explicitly want server-fetch-driven updates.

Query Records nodes observing the class see the record leave their results automatically.
enrichment.whenToUse: Destructive removal of cloud records. If the product needs undo or soft delete, model an 'archived' flag with Set Record Properties instead — deletion is final.

enrichment.summary: Makes its child subtree draggable along X and/or Y, reporting position and drag signals, with animated snap-to-position.
enrichment.description: Drag is a visual container: whatever you place inside it can be dragged with the pointer. `axis` restricts movement ('x' by default, 'y' or 'both'), `enabled` turns dragging on/off, and `useParentBounds` (Constrain to parent, default true) keeps the content inside its parent's box. While dragging, `positionX`/`positionY` (Drag X/Y) hold the current offset in pixels and `deltaX`/`deltaY` the per-move change; `onStart` (Drag Started), `onDrag` (Drag Moved) and `onStop` (Drag Ended) are signals bracketing the gesture. The position can also be driven from the graph: setting `inputPositionX`/`inputPositionY` (Start Drag X/Y) moves the content and updates the outputs, and the `snapToPositionX.do`/`snapToPositionY.do` signals animate to `snapToPositionX.value` over `snapToPositionX.duration` milliseconds (default 300).
enrichment.whenToUse: Sliders, swipeable cards, drawers, reorder handles — any direct-manipulation gesture where you need the live drag offset. For scrolling content use a Group with scrolling enabled instead; for purely programmatic motion use an Animation on a node's Pos X/Y rather than a Drag no one touches.

ports.axis: Enum value: 'x' (default), 'y' or 'both' — which axes the pointer can move the content along.
ports.useParentBounds: Boolean value (Constrain to parent, default true); keeps the dragged content within the parent element's bounds.
ports.inputPositionX: Number value (Start Drag X); writing it repositions the content programmatically and re-emits `positionX`/`deltaX`.
ports.scale: Number value (default 1); set it when the drag area is visually scaled so pointer movement maps 1:1 to position.
ports.snapToPositionX.do: Signal; animates the X position to `snapToPositionX.value` over `snapToPositionX.duration` ms. Starting a new drag cancels the animation.
ports.positionX: Number value (Drag X): current X offset in pixels; keeps its last value after the gesture ends.
ports.deltaX: Number value (Delta X): change in X since the previous drag event — useful for velocity-style logic.
ports.onStop: Signal (Drag Ended); fires when the pointer releases — the usual place to decide whether to snap back or snap to a slot.

patterns: Snap back: `onStop` → `snapToPositionX.do` with `snapToPositionX.value` 0 — released content animates home.
Swipe threshold: `positionX` → Expression/Condition deciding on `onStop` whether to snap to the open or closed position.
antiPatterns: Rebuilding a scroll view out of Drag — a Group with scrolling enabled handles momentum, wheel and touch for free.

enrichment.summary: Receive Event: fires when a Send Event broadcasts on the same channel, delivering the event's payload values as outputs.
enrichment.description: Event Receiver listens on `channelName` and fires its `eventReceived` signal each time an Event Sender sends on that channel, from anywhere in the app. Payload values declared by the sender appear as value outputs holding the payload of the most recent event. `enabled` mutes the receiver; `consume` controls whether this receiver swallows the event or lets other receivers on the channel also fire.
enrichment.whenToUse: The reacting end of decoupled notifications: refresh triggers, toasts, logout cleanup. For parent↔child flow use Component Inputs/Outputs; for continuously-shared state use Variables/Objects.

ports.eventReceived: Signal; fires once per received event, after the payload outputs have been updated.

patterns: `eventReceived` → a query's fetch input: app-wide refresh without wiring panels together.
antiPatterns: Reading payload outputs outside the moment of the event as if they were state — they hold only the last event's values; use a Variable/Object for state.

enrichment.summary: Send Event: broadcasts a named event, with optional payload values, to every Receive Event listening on the same channel.
enrichment.description: Event Sender fires an app-wide (or scoped) event when its `sendEvent` signal triggers. The event is identified by `channelName`; every Event Receiver with the same channel fires in response, wherever it lives in the component tree — no wires between them. Payload values are declared on the `payload` parameter (a list of names); each declared name becomes an input port whose current value travels with the event and appears as an output on the receivers. `propagation` narrows delivery (e.g. to parent components only) instead of broadcasting globally.
enrichment.whenToUse: Cross-cutting notifications where sender and receivers must stay decoupled: 'refresh now', 'user logged out', toast requests. For parent↔child communication prefer Component Inputs/Outputs; for shared state prefer Variables/Objects — events are moments, not state.

ports.sendEvent: Signal; fires the event once per trigger.
ports.channelName: The event's name; matching is exact and case-sensitive with receivers.
ports.payload: Comma-separated list of payload value names; each becomes an input port carried with the event.
ports.propagation: Delivery scope: notify all receivers, only those in parent components, etc. Default notifies all.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: Runtime-discovered inputs: each name listed in `payload` is registered as an input port on demand. The payload port set is defined entirely by that parameter and cannot be known without it.
patterns: Toolbar button → Send Event('RefreshRequested'); data panels each hold a Receive Event that re-runs their query.
Payload-carrying events for 'open item X' style requests, received where the detail view lives.
antiPatterns: Using events as a data bus for continuously-changing values — receivers only see values at event time; use a Variable/Object for state.
Free-typing slightly different channel names at each end; channel matching is exact.

dynamicPorts.description: Input ports are created for each free variable referenced in the "expression" parameter (e.g. the expression "a + b" yields number inputs named "a" and "b"). The "result" output and its type follow the expression.

variables.expression: a free variable referenced in the `expression` parameter

enrichment.summary: Evaluates a one-line JavaScript expression whose free variables become input ports; outputs the result as value, boolean, string and events.
enrichment.description: Expression compiles the JavaScript expression in its `expression` parameter and re-evaluates it whenever any referenced input changes (or only on the `run` signal, if `run` is connected). Every free variable name in the expression text becomes an input port of that name — write `price * quantity` and the node grows `price` and `quantity` inputs. The result is exposed simultaneously as `result` (untyped), `asNumber`, `asString`, `asBoolean`, plus level booleans `isTrue`/`isFalse` and edge signals `isTrueEv`/`isFalseEv` that fire when the truthiness changes.
enrichment.whenToUse: Small computations and predicates inline in a graph: arithmetic, comparisons, string interpolation via template syntax, ternaries. For multi-statement logic, side effects, or async work use the Function node; for combining two booleans And/Or are clearer.

ports.expression: The expression source text. Its identifiers define the node's data inputs; standard Math functions are available (e.g. round(), abs()).
ports.run: Signal; when connected, the expression stops auto-evaluating on input changes and evaluates only when this fires.
ports.result: Untyped output ('*') carrying the raw value — connectable to any input, so type discipline is on the author.
ports.isTrueEv: Signal; fires when an evaluation turns the result truthy — an edge, unlike the `isTrue` level.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: Inputs are runtime-discovered by parsing the expression text: each identifier that is not a built-in becomes an input port registered on demand. The port set therefore changes whenever the expression is edited, and cannot be known without the expression. Reads of Noodl.Variables/Objects inside the expression additionally subscribe the node to those stores.
patterns: Input validation: text ports feed an Expression predicate; its `result` drives a Condition's `condition`.
Derived display values: `asString` → a Text's `text` for computed captions.
antiPatterns: Chaining many Expression nodes to build a program — one Function node with readable JavaScript beats a lattice of expressions.
Side effects in the expression; it may evaluate more often than you expect. Expressions must stay pure.

enrichment.summary: Array Filter: filters, sorts and limits an input array into a new output array, re-running automatically when the source changes.
enrichment.description: Takes an array on `items`, applies the filter, sort and limit configured in its parameters, and outputs the result as a new array on `items` — the input array is never mutated, and each run produces a fresh array object. It re-runs automatically whenever the input array's contents change, unless the `filter` (Filter) signal input is connected, in which case filtering happens only when that signal fires. With `enabled` false the input passes through unfiltered (still as a copy). After each run `modified` (Filtered) fires and `count`/`firstItemId` describe the output. Filter operators: eq/neq for all types, lt/gt/lte/gte for numbers, regex (with optional case sensitivity) for strings.
enrichment.whenToUse: Client-side filtering, searching and sorting of arrays already in memory — e.g. a live search box over a Static Array or shared Array. For server data prefer filtering in the Query Records node so the database does the work; for reshaping item properties use Array Map.

ports.items: Input (value): the source array. Output (value): a new filtered/sorted array — this is what you feed a Repeater.
ports.filter: Signal input; when connected, disables automatic re-filtering and runs the filter only on this signal.
ports.enabled: Boolean value; false passes the input through without filtering, sorting or limiting.
ports.modified: Signal (Filtered); fires after each filter run.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior:
The filter/sort/limit configuration creates its own input ports, pushed to the editor per instance: `filterFilter` (a stringlist of property names) generates, per property

, `filterFilterType-

` (string/number/boolean), `filterFilterOp-

` (eq, neq, regex for strings; eq, neq, lt, gt, gte, lte for numbers), `filterFilterValue-

` (a connectable value — wire a text input here for live search) and, for regex, `filterFilterOption-case-

`. `filterSort` (stringlist) generates `filterSort-

` (ascending/descending) per property. `filterEnableLimit` (boolean) reveals `filterLimit` (default 10) and `filterSkip` (default 0). An authoring tool must set `filterFilter`/`filterSort` first and use exactly these generated names.
patterns: Static Array or Array `items` → Array Filter `items` → Repeater `items`: a filtered local list.
Text Input `text` → `filterFilterValue-<prop>` with op regex: live search-as-you-type.
antiPatterns: Filtering large cloud datasets client-side — put the filter in Query Records instead so only matching records are fetched.

dynamicPorts.description: Filter input ports are generated by the editor from the visual filter definition (FilterRecordsAdapter) and the selected class schema.

parameterEncoding.reason: The port helper could not be run headlessly — it needs project context this generator does not have (Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'find')).

enrichment.summary: Filter Records: applies a visual filter/sort/limit to an already-fetched array of records, client-side.
enrichment.description: Filter Records narrows and orders an `items` array of records without touching the server: the filter, sorting and limit are configured on the node exactly like Query Records' visual filter, but evaluated locally against the incoming array. The result comes out on `items` with `count` alongside; `modified` fires when the output recomputes. Use `filter` (signal) to re-evaluate on demand and `enabled` to bypass.
enrichment.whenToUse: Deriving multiple views from one fetched result set — tabs, local search-as-you-type, secondary sorts — without re-querying. When the full data set should never reach the client, filter in the query itself (Query Records) instead.

ports.items: Records in (input) and the filtered, sorted subset out (output).
ports.enabled: Boolean; when false the input passes through unfiltered.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: Filter-value inputs are generated from the visual filter you build in the editor (each 'value' placeholder becomes an input port) — runtime-discovered + editor-adapter, same mechanism as Query Records.
patterns: One Query Records fanned into several Filter Records: one fetch, many live views.
antiPatterns: Client-filtering an unlimited query as a substitute for server-side where/limit — the full class still crosses the network.

parameterEncoding.reason: Input ports mirror the input ports of the template component chosen by the `template` parameter, name for name. They cannot be derived from this node's own parameters.

enrichment.summary: Repeater: instantiates a template component once per item of an input array, inserting the instances as children at its position.
enrichment.description: The Repeater consumes an array on `items` and creates one instance of its template component per item, placed into the visual tree where the Repeater sits (it must therefore be a child of a visual container). With `templateType` explicit (the default) the template is one component chosen on the `template` input; with `templateType` dynamic, a `templateScript` chooses a component per item at runtime. Item data flows into each instance through the instance's Component Inputs whose names match the item object's property names. The repeater diffs changes to the array, adding/removing instances rather than rebuilding everything.
enrichment.whenToUse: Any repeated UI: lists, grids, menus, table rows. Its idiomatic partner is Query Records for cloud data or a Static Data/Variable2 array for local data. Not for repeating pure logic without visuals — see For Each Actions.

ports.items: The array to repeat over. Each element should be an object; its properties feed the item component's matching Component Inputs.
ports.template: The item component (visible when `templateType` is explicit). Component names start with '/'; components in a sheet are '/#Sheet Name/Component Name'.
ports.templateScript: JavaScript choosing a component per item (visible when `templateType` is dynamic): set `component` using the `item` variable.
ports.refresh: Signal; tears down and rebuilds all instances. Rarely needed — the repeater tracks array changes itself.
ports.itemActionItemId: Outputs the id of the item whose instance triggered a For Each Actions flow.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: Two dynamic mechanisms: `template`/`templateScript` swap in and out based on `templateType` (declared-port-groups), and outputs named after signals sent by item components are registered on demand (runtime-discovered) — an item component's Component Outputs signal appears as an output port here so a list can bubble events up.
patterns: Query Records `items` → Repeater `items`: the canonical data-driven list.
Item component declares Component Inputs matching record property names — no explicit per-field wiring at the list level.
antiPatterns: Triggering `refresh` whenever data changes: the repeater already diffs `items`; refresh forces a full rebuild and loses instance state.
Binding huge unpaged query results into a repeater; page or limit the query instead.

enrichment.summary: Repeater Item: inside a repeater's item component, exposes this row's item id and its add/remove lifecycle.
enrichment.description: Repeater Item gives an item component access to its own position in the enclosing Repeater. `itemId` outputs the id of the object this instance renders — the key that lets row-level actions target row-level data. `added` fires when the instance enters the list; `tryRemove` initiates this row's removal, with `removeCompleted` letting an exit animation finish before the instance is destroyed.
enrichment.whenToUse: Any per-row behaviour in a repeated component: writing back to the row's object, removal buttons, staggered entrance/exit animation. Outside a repeater item component the node has nothing to bind to.

ports.itemId: The id of this row's item object; wire into Object/Set Object Properties `modelId` or bubble it out via Component Outputs.
ports.tryRemove: Signal output firing when removal of this row is requested — run your exit animation, then confirm.
ports.removeCompleted: Signal input; confirms removal after `tryRemove`, letting the repeater delete the instance.

patterns: `itemId` → Set Object Properties `modelId`: row edits write to exactly this row (27 occurrences in the real-project corpus).

enrichment.summary: The universal layout container: a flexbox div that stacks its children in a row or column and is the root of most components.
enrichment.description: Group is the workhorse visual container. It renders as a flexbox element and lays out its visual children (the `children` list in the project file) along `flexDirection`, with alignment, padding, margins, size, scrolling, borders and background as parameters. Nearly every component's visual tree starts with a Group; nesting Groups is how all layout is composed. It also reports interaction (`onClick`, hover and pointer signals) and geometry (`boundingWidth`/`boundingHeight`, screen position), so it doubles as a click surface.
enrichment.whenToUse: Reach for Group whenever you need structure: rows, columns, cards, overlays, scroll areas, click targets. Do not use it for text (use Text), images (Image), or button-like affordances with label/icon styling (net.noodl.controls.button).

ports.flexDirection: Layout axis for children: 'row' or 'column' (column is the default).
ports.clip: When true, children are clipped to the Group's bounds — required for most scroll containers.
ports.onClick: Signal; fires on click/tap of the group surface. Any Group can act as a button.
ports.didMount: Signal; fires when the group enters the render tree — a common 'component is ready' trigger.
ports.this: Reference to the visual object itself, consumed by nodes that need a target reference (e.g. Animation targets).
ports.onScrollPositionChanged: Number level with the current scroll offset while scrolling is enabled.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: Group's port list is largely static, but several port groups are conditional on parameter values (declared-port-groups): scroll-related ports appear when scrolling is enabled, advanced-dimension ports depend on the size mode, and visual-state variants add ports per state. An authoring tool should treat the catalog's input list as the superset and expect the editor to expose subsets based on the node's current parameters.
patterns: Component root: a single Group at the top of every visual component, `flexDirection` column.
Scroll list: outer Group with scrolling enabled and `clip` true, Repeater inside.
antiPatterns: Deeply nesting a Group per style tweak; set padding/margins on the existing Group instead.

enrichment.summary: Displays an image from a project asset or URL, with fit control, srcSet support and load/error signals.
enrichment.description: Image renders an HTML `img` element. `src` takes a project asset path or a full URL (relative paths are resolved against the app's base URL); `srcSet` optionally provides responsive candidate images and `alt` the accessibility text. When `sizeMode` gives the image an explicit size, `objectFit` (Image Fit) chooses how the picture fills that box ('contain' by default, 'cover' for thumbnails). `onLoad` and `onError` are signals that fire when the browser finishes or fails loading the current source. It cannot have children and supports hover visual states for per-state styling.
enrichment.whenToUse: Any bitmap content: photos, thumbnails, logos, user uploads (a cloud file output connects straight to `src`). For vector glyphs from an icon set use net.noodl.visual.icon; for a decorative background prefer a Group's background image/color so children can sit on top; for video use Video.

ports.src: Image value: a project asset path or URL. This is the only image input that matters in most graphs — bind record data or a cloud file here.
ports.srcSet: String value in HTML `srcset` syntax for responsive images; when set it takes precedence in the inspector and lets the browser pick a candidate.
ports.alt: String value read by screen readers and shown if the image cannot load; empty by default, set it for meaningful images.
ports.objectFit: Enum (Image Fit): how the bitmap fills an explicitly sized box — 'contain' (default), 'cover', 'fill', 'none', 'scale-down'. Only present when the size mode gives the node explicit dimensions.
ports.onLoad: Signal; fires when the current `src` has finished loading — useful to fade the image in.
ports.onError: Signal; fires when loading fails — swap in a placeholder source here.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: Declared-port-groups: `objectFit`, `width` and `height` appear based on `sizeMode`; per-side border width/color ports appear once a border style is chosen; box-shadow ports appear when `boxShadowEnabled` is true; `pointerEventsEnabled` appears when `pointerEventsMode` is 'explicit'. Treat the catalog's input list as the superset the editor filters by current parameters.
patterns: Inside a Repeater item component: Component Inputs property → `src` to show per-record images.
Thumbnail grid: explicit size mode + `objectFit` 'cover' so mixed aspect ratios crop instead of distort.
antiPatterns: Using Image for icon-font glyphs — net.noodl.visual.icon renders them sharper and tintable via `iconColor`.

inputs.description: Value to negate; anything falsy counts as false, and leaving it unset keeps Result unset too

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: The opposite of Value, and unset rather than true while Value has never been set

enrichment.summary: Logical NOT: outputs the boolean opposite of its input.
enrichment.description: Inverter takes one boolean `value` (Value) input and exposes its negation on the `result` (Result) value output. Until the input has received a value, the result is undefined rather than true — the node does not invent a state before it has one. Any change to the input immediately updates the result. It has no signals and no configuration.
enrichment.whenToUse: Use it wherever you have the boolean you need, but backwards — e.g. a Switch's `state` drives a panel's `visible` and, inverted, a placeholder's `visible`. If the boolean comes from a Condition, prefer its built-in `isfalse` output and skip the Inverter. For combining several booleans, use And/Or or an Expression.

ports.result: Boolean value: the opposite of `value`. Undefined until `value` first receives data.

patterns: A 'is loading' boolean → Inverter → a button's `enabled`: disable actions while busy.
Switch `state` → Inverter → the collapsed view's `visible`: show exactly one of two views from a single boolean.
antiPatterns: Chaining Condition → Inverter to get 'is false' — Condition already outputs `isfalse` directly.

dynamicPorts.description: This is the Function node. Input and output ports are discovered from the user script in the "functionScript" parameter: reading "Inputs.xyz" creates input port "xyz", assigning "Outputs.xyz" creates output port "xyz". Signal outputs are created by calling "Outputs.xyz()".

variables.functionScript: a name read as `Inputs.<name>` or assigned as `Outputs.<name>` in the `functionScript` parameter

variables.scriptInput: the `label` of a row in the `scriptInputs` parameter
the `label` of a row in the `scriptInputs` parameter

variables.scriptOutput: the `label` of a row in the `scriptOutputs` parameter
the `label` of a row in the `scriptOutputs` parameter

parameterEncoding.notes: Names are interpolated verbatim, including spaces — a value called `bg color` produces a port called `value-true-bg color`, not `value-true-bgColor`.

enrichment.summary: Function: runs multi-line JavaScript; Inputs.* reads create input ports, Outputs.* writes create output ports, Outputs.fn() fires signals.
enrichment.description: The Function node executes the JavaScript in `functionScript`. The script's surface *is* its port list: reading `Inputs.name` creates an input port `name`, assigning `Outputs.name = value` creates a value output, and calling `Outputs.name()` creates and fires a signal output (conventionally `Outputs.Success()` / `Outputs.Failure()`). The script runs when the `run` signal fires; if `run` is unconnected it runs whenever a connected input changes. Scripts may be async and use `await` — fire a signal output when done to sequence downstream work.
enrichment.whenToUse: Anything beyond a one-liner: data transformation, calling browser APIs or fetch, orchestrating async steps. Prefer Expression for simple pure computations and dedicated nodes (Query Records, REST2) where they exist — graphs stay more inspectable than scripts.

ports.functionScript: The JavaScript source. Its Inputs./Outputs. references define the node's data and signal ports.
ports.run: Signal; executes the script. When connected, input changes no longer auto-run the script.
ports.scriptInputs: Editor-managed list of the input ports the script declares — not authored directly.
ports.scriptOutputs: Editor-managed list of the output ports the script declares — not authored directly.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: All data/signal ports are runtime-discovered from the script source: the editor parses `Inputs.x` / `Outputs.y` references (JavascriptNodeParser) and registers matching ports; nothing about them is static. An authoring tool must write the script first and then wire to exactly the names the script uses — including signal outputs, which are the calls, not assignments.

enrichment.summary: Script: runs JavaScript that declares its own typed inputs/outputs, named signal handlers and lifecycle (setup/run/destroy) methods.
enrichment.description: The Script node executes the JavaScript in its `code` parameter (or, when `useExternalFile` is `yes`, a file fetched from `externalFile`). Unlike the Function node, the script declares its ports explicitly and gets a lifecycle: `define({ inputs: { price: 'number' }, outputs: { total: 'number' }, setup: fn, run: fn, destroy: fn, mySignal: fn })` creates typed input/output ports from the `inputs`/`outputs` maps, runs `setup` once after the code is parsed, runs `run` (alias `change`) each time any value input changes (it receives `(inputs, outputs, changedInputs)`), runs a function named after a signal input when that signal fires, and runs `destroy` when the node is removed. A newer `script({...})` form adds `signals: {}`, `changed: {}` (per-input change handlers) and `methods: {}` sections. Inside handlers, `this.flagOutputDirty(name)` and `this.sendSignalOnOutput(name)` push results out. Typed ports can also be added from the editor panel via the `scriptInputs`/`scriptOutputs` lists.
enrichment.whenToUse: Use Script when code needs a real lifecycle — initialize a library or subscription in `setup`, tear it down in `destroy` — or several distinct signal entry points with typed ports. For ordinary run-once logic and async calls, prefer JavaScriptFunction (Function): its implicit `Inputs.x`/`Outputs.y` ports and single `run` signal are simpler. For pure one-liners use Expression.

ports.code: The script source (edit-only). Its declared `inputs`/`outputs` maps and signal-handler names define the node's ports.
ports.useExternalFile: Edit-only enum; `yes` swaps the `code` port for `externalFile` and loads the script from a project file at runtime.
ports.externalFile: Edit-only path to a script file; the node stays inert until the file has loaded and parsed.
ports.scriptInputs: Editor-managed list adding typed input ports (with a Type selector per entry) alongside those declared in code.
ports.scriptOutputs: Editor-managed list adding typed output ports alongside those declared in code.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: All data and signal ports are runtime-discovered by parsing the script (JavascriptNodeParser): the keys of the declared `inputs`/`outputs` maps become ports with the declared types, each `signals` entry (or top-level handler function named like a signal input) becomes a signal input, and entries in the `scriptInputs`/`scriptOutputs` proplist parameters add further typed ports. Nothing about the port set is static — an authoring tool must write the script first and wire only names the script (or the proplists) declares. When `useExternalFile` is `yes` the ports come from the downloaded file, so they are unknowable until it loads.
patterns: Wrap a stateful browser library: instantiate it in `setup`, feed it from `changed` handlers, dispose it in `destroy`.
Declare `mySignal: function (inputs, outputs) {...}` and wire a Button `onClick` to the `mySignal` input for an explicit, named action entry point.
antiPatterns: Using Script for a simple transform that reruns on input change — the Function node does that with less ceremony.
Assigning outputs without the declared `outputs` entry: undeclared names never become ports.
