enrichment.summary: Block-based (Blockly) logic: blocks compile to JavaScript that runs when a signal fires and writes the node's output ports.
enrichment.description: Logic Builder stores a visual block program (Google Blockly) in its `workspace` parameter; the editor generates plain JavaScript from the blocks into the hidden `generatedCode` parameter, and the runtime compiles and executes that code. Execution is strictly signal-driven: the logic runs when the `run` signal input (or a block-defined signal input) fires — changing an input value alone never executes it. The generated code runs with `Inputs`, `Outputs`, `Noodl`, `Variables`, `Objects`, `Arrays` and `sendSignalOnOutput` in scope, so blocks can read and write global Noodl Variables/Objects/Arrays. Every `Outputs["name"] = ...` in the program becomes a value output that updates after each run; a runtime exception lands in the `error` string output.
enrichment.whenToUse: Reach for it when logic must be authorable without writing JavaScript. For anything beyond what the block set expresses — async work, loops over API data, library calls — use JavaScriptFunction (Function); for a one-line computation use Expression.

ports.run: Signal input (connections only, hidden in the property panel); fires one execution of the block program.
ports.workspace: Edit-only Blockly workspace JSON, authored in the block editor — not written by hand.
ports.generatedCode: Edit-only JavaScript the editor generates from the blocks; the runtime executes exactly this text.
ports.error: String value output holding the message of the last execution error, empty when the last run succeeded.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: Ports are runtime-determined from the generated code: the editor scans `generatedCode` for `Outputs["name"]` assignments and publishes a value output per name (it publishes ports only when at least one output is detected). Input, signal-input and signal-output detection is not currently implemented in the editor's port scan, so data must reach the program through Noodl Variables/Objects rather than input connections; the runtime would register input ports on demand, but the editor does not surface them. An authoring tool should treat `workspace`/`generatedCode` as editor-managed, wire signals to `run`, and read only outputs that appear as `Outputs["..."]` in the generated code.
patterns: Button `onClick` → `run`, with an `Outputs["..."]` value wired to a Text — the minimal block-program shape.
Blocks read and write `Noodl.Variables` to exchange state with the rest of the app instead of using input ports.
antiPatterns: Expecting the logic to re-run when connected values change — nothing executes until a signal fires.
Hand-editing `generatedCode`; the block editor overwrites it from `workspace`.

enrichment.summary: Array Map: transforms each element of an input array with a map script, emitting a new array and leaving the source untouched.
enrichment.description: Array Map runs its `mapScript` once per element of `items` — the script calls `map(...)` with the reshaped object, with the current element available as `object` — and outputs the resulting new array. The transformation is non-destructive and re-runs when the input array changes, so it behaves like a live derived view.
enrichment.whenToUse: Reshaping list data between its source and the UI: computing display labels, renaming properties, deriving fields. For narrowing a list use Array Filter; for arbitrary multi-array logic a Function node is clearer than a chain of maps.

antiPatterns: Mutating `object` inside the map script — emit a new shape via map(); mutation writes through to the shared source objects.

enrichment.summary: Object: binds to one client-side object by id and exposes its properties reactively; the shared store behind repeater items and app state.
enrichment.description: Object (Model2) is a window onto one object in the client-side object store. Bind it via `modelId` (or, per `idSource`, the enclosing repeater item) and the properties declared on the node become value outputs that update whenever anything writes the object — Set Object Properties, cloud-data nodes, scripts. `changed` fires on each such write. Objects are shared by id: every Object node with the same id sees the same data, which is how unconnected parts of a graph stay in sync.

enrichment.summary: Close Popup: dismisses the popup this node lives in, sending named results and a close action back to the opener.
enrichment.description: Close Popup works only inside a component shown via Show Popup: when `close` fires it removes the overlay. The `results` list declares values handed back (each becomes an input here and an output on the Show Popup node), and `closeActions` declares named reasons, each surfacing as its own signal at the opener — the mechanism for confirm/cancel semantics.
enrichment.whenToUse: Every dismissal affordance inside a popup: confirm buttons, cancel crosses, backdrop clicks (via the backdrop Group's onClick). It has no effect outside a popup.

ports.results: Declared result names; each becomes a value input carried to the opener.
ports.closeActions: Named close reasons; each appears as a signal output on the opener's Show Popup node.

enrichment.summary: Show Popup: overlays a component on top of the app when triggered; the popup closes itself and can hand back results.
enrichment.description: Show Popup instantiates `target` (a component) as an overlay above everything else when `show` fires. The popup component owns its dismissal: a Close Popup node inside it removes the overlay, fires this node's `Closed` signal, and delivers any declared result values as outputs here — plus one signal output per close action, so 'confirmed' and 'dismissed' can be told apart at the call site.
enrichment.whenToUse: Dialogs, sheets, confirmations — transient UI that must sit above the page and return an answer. For a persistent section of the page, conditional `mounted` on a Group is lighter; for full pages use Router or Component Stack.

ports.target: The component shown as the overlay.
ports.Closed: Signal; fires when the popup closed, after result outputs update.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: Result-value outputs and per-close-action signals are generated from the Close Popup configuration inside the target component; the target's Component Inputs also surface as inputs here. All of it is project-content-determined.
patterns: Confirmation dialog: show → popup's confirm/cancel close actions → distinct signals at the caller.
antiPatterns: Closing a popup from outside it — dismissal belongs inside the popup component, where Close Popup works.

enrichment.summary: Create New Record: inserts a record into a cloud database class from its property inputs when Do is triggered.
enrichment.description: NewDbModelProperties (Create New Record) creates one record in the cloud database class chosen with the `collectionName` (Class) parameter. Each property of the class becomes a value input; when the `store` (Do) signal is triggered, the current input values are sent to the server as a new record. On success the node binds to the new record, outputs its `id`, and fires `created` (Success); on failure it fires `failure` with a message on `error`. Optionally, `sourceObjectId` seeds the new record with the data of an existing local object (explicit property inputs win), and Access Control Rules restrict who can read/write the record (defaulting to the creating user when a rule is left unconfigured).
enrichment.whenToUse: The write half of every 'add item' flow — forms, quick-add buttons, duplicating a record via `sourceObjectId`. Live Query Records nodes pick the new record up automatically, so no manual re-fetch is needed. To modify an existing record use SetDbModelProperties instead; for a non-cloud (BYOB) backend use noodl.byob.CreateRecord.

ports.store: Signal (displayed as Do); performs the insert using the property input values current at that moment.
ports.created: Signal (displayed as Success); fires after the server confirms the insert. The `id` output is valid from here on.
ports.id: String value; the id of the created record — feed it to a Record node or navigation parameter.
ports.sourceObjectId: Value input (connections only): id of a local object/record whose data seeds the new record before the property inputs are applied.
ports.accessControl: Edit-only list of access rules; each rule expands into its own Target/Read/Write inputs (see runtimeBehavior). With no rules the record gets the class default (public) permissions.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: Ports are runtime-determined: `collectionName` (Class) is registered as an edit-only enum of the project's classes plus _User/_Role, and each schema property of the chosen class becomes a value input `prop-<name>` typed from the schema. Each entry in the `accessControl` list additionally spawns `acl-<ruleId>-target` (user/everyone/role), then `acl-<ruleId>-userid` or `acl-<ruleId>-role`, plus `acl-<ruleId>-read` and `acl-<ruleId>-write` booleans. An authoring tool should set `collectionName` in parameters and drive `prop-<name>` inputs it knows from the class schema.
patterns: Text Input `text` → `prop-<name>`, Button `onClick` → `store`: the minimal create form.
`created` → a navigation or Event Sender, with `id` as payload: jump straight to the new record's detail page.
antiPatterns: Re-fetching a Query Records node after `created` — live queries already receive the new record; only re-fetch when the query is not live.

enrichment.summary: Create New Object: creates a new client-side object with the declared properties set and outputs the new object's id.
enrichment.description: Create New Object makes a new object in the app's client-side object store when the `new` (Do) signal fires. Objects are in-memory key/value records addressable by id from anywhere in the app — Object (Model2) nodes, Set Object Properties, repeaters and Component Inputs all bind to the same store. Which properties the new object gets is declared in the `properties` parameter; each declared name becomes a value input whose current value is written onto the object at creation time. After creation the object's id is available on the `id` output and `created` (Done) fires — creation is deferred until all inputs updated in the same cycle have settled, so payload values wired alongside the trigger are included.
enrichment.whenToUse: Use it to mint new client-side state records: items added to a local list, draft objects before saving, per-session working data. Objects are in-memory only — for persistent cloud data use the record nodes (e.g. Create New Record / NewDbModelProperties) instead; for a single named value a Variable (Variable2) is simpler.

ports.new: Signal input; schedules creation after pending input updates, then creates the object, writes the declared properties and fires `created`.
ports.created: Signal; fires once per creation, after the object exists and its properties are set.
ports.id: String value; the id of the most recently created object. Feed it to Object (Model2) or Set Object Properties `modelId` to keep working with it.
ports.properties: Edit-only stringlist declaring the property names to set; each name becomes a `prop-<name>` input.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior:
Property inputs are runtime-discovered from the `properties` parameter: each declared name p produces a value input `prop-

` (group Property Values) and an edit-only enum `type-

` (String/Boolean/Number/Date/Array/Object/Any, default Any). At creation each declared property receives its input value, or a type-based default (false, empty string, 0, current date) when no value was provided. Array-typed values given as strings are evaluated as JavaScript literals; object-typed values given as strings are resolved as object ids. An authoring tool must set `properties` first — the `prop-`/`type-` ports do not exist without it.
patterns: Receive Event payload outputs → `prop-` inputs, `eventReceived` → `new`: create an object from an event's payload.
`id` → Set Object Properties `modelId`: continue mutating the object you just created.
antiPatterns: Expecting created objects to persist — the object store is client-side and in-memory; reloading the app clears it. Use cloud record nodes for persistence.

inputs.name: treatEmptyAs
inputs.description: Back-compat for graphs written before Variables were nullable. `null` (default) keeps a cleared value distinguishable from a real 0. Choosing another option restores the pre-NDA-003 coercion for authors who relied on it.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The empty-value contract (dev-docs/reference/EMPTY-VALUE-CONTRACT.md): `undefined` abstains and leaves the Variable's stored value untouched. `null` is a real value — it clears the Variable, is stored, and fires Changed. What "cleared" is stored as is controlled by `Treat empty as` (null by default).

outputs.name: savedValue
outputs.description: Can be `null` — a cleared Variable (see `value`'s description) stores and emits null by default, not this type's zero value, unless `Treat empty as` says otherwise.

enrichment.summary: Per-instance numeric holder: stores one number locally, optionally latching new values until a Set signal fires.
enrichment.description: Number holds a single numeric value that belongs to this node instance alone — it is not named or shared (for an app-wide named value use Variable2). The `value` input sets it and `savedValue` (Value) reads it back. While the `saveValue` (Set) signal input is unconnected, values written to `value` apply immediately; once `saveValue` is connected the node latches: incoming values are held pending and only applied when Set fires. Incoming values are cast with JavaScript Number(), so non-numeric strings become NaN. `changed` fires only when the stored value actually changes; `stored` fires after every Set trigger.
enrichment.whenToUse: Use it to hold a local number — a counter, an index, a captured measurement — especially with the latch: feed a computed value into `value` and commit it with Set at the moment of an action. For simple increment/decrement a Counter is less wiring; for app-wide numbers use Variable2 + Set Variable.

ports.value: Number value input. Applies immediately when `saveValue` is unconnected; otherwise held until Set fires.
ports.saveValue: Signal; applies the most recently received `value`, then fires `stored`. Connecting it switches the node from pass-through to latch mode.
ports.savedValue: Number level with the currently stored value.
ports.changed: Signal; fires only when the stored value actually changes.
ports.stored: Signal; fires after every Set trigger, even when the value did not change.

patterns: Counter loop: `savedValue` → an Expression (`count + 1`) → `value`, with a click signal on `saveValue` — each click commits the incremented value. The latch prevents an infinite feedback loop.
`savedValue` → a Text's `text`: numbers cast to strings on delivery, so the count renders directly.
antiPatterns: Wiring `savedValue` through an Expression back into `value` without connecting `saveValue` — with no latch the loop applies immediately and the value is unstable. Connect Set and drive it from a signal.

outputs.description: Input Value rescaled from the input range onto the output range

enrichment.summary: Linearly maps a number from one range to another, optionally clamped — e.g. 0–100 progress to 0–1 opacity.
enrichment.description: Number Remapper converts `inputValue` (Input Value) from the input range [`minInputValue` (Input Minimum), `maxInputValue` (Input Maximum)] to the output range [`minOutputValue` (Output Minimum, default 0), `maxOutputValue` (Output Maximum, default 1)] with straight linear interpolation, writing the result to the `remappedValue` (Remapped Value) number output. With `clamp` (Clamp Output, default true) the normalized position is limited to 0…1 so the output never leaves the output range; with clamping off, values outside the input range extrapolate. Ranges may be inverted (min greater than max) to reverse direction. If the input range is empty (minimum equals maximum) the output is pinned to `minOutputValue`. Every input recomputes the output immediately.
enrichment.whenToUse: The no-code way to scale a value between domains: a count to a progress-bar width, a scroll position to an opacity, a slider value to a rotation. For non-linear curves or multi-input math use Expression or a Function.

ports.inputValue: Number value to remap; connection-only, it cannot be set as a parameter.
ports.clamp: Boolean, parameter-only (default true): keeps the output inside the output range. Disable to extrapolate beyond it.
ports.remappedValue: Number value output; equals `minOutputValue` whenever the input range is empty (Input Minimum = Input Maximum).

patterns: Counter `currentCount` → `inputValue` with the output range sized in pixels → a Group's `width`: a value-driven fill bar.
Scroll position → `inputValue`, output range 1…0 → `opacity`: fade an element out as the user scrolls.
antiPatterns: Leaving Input Minimum and Input Maximum both at 0 — the output sits at Output Minimum no matter what comes in; set a real input range.

outputs.name: message

outputs.name: nodeId

outputs.name: nodeType

enrichment.summary: App-wide error boundary: fires whenever any node reports a failure, with the code, message and the node it came from.
enrichment.description: The catch-all half of the Failure Contract. Per-node `Failure` outputs cover the errors an author expects and wants to branch on where they happen; this node covers everything else, which is most of them — the library will never carry complete failure ports on all 155 node types, and without a boundary the only record of an unwired error is a console line nobody sees in a deployed app. It subscribes as soon as it is created, so errors raised while the graph is still starting up are caught too. `Filter` narrows it by code prefix: blank catches everything, `run-tasks` catches every failure Run Tasks can report, `run-tasks/no-completion-output` catches exactly one. Several instances can coexist and all of them fire — this is a boundary, not a handler chain, so one node logging every error never stops another from showing a toast for the subset it cares about.
enrichment.whenToUse: Put one in the app's root component to make failures visible at all — log them, show a message, or forward `Error Object` to an error-reporting service. Add narrower ones with a `Filter` where a particular area needs its own handling. Use a node's own `Failure` output instead when you want to branch on an error at the point it happens.

ports.filter: Blank is the useful default for a boundary; a code prefix narrows it to one node type or one specific error.
ports.error: Value outputs are updated before this fires, so reading Message or Code on the pulse always describes this error.
ports.errorObject: Wireable straight into a string input, which renders it as JSON.

patterns: One unfiltered On App Error in the root component, with `Message` into a Text and `Error` showing a popup — the minimum that makes a deployed app's failures visible.
`Error Object` into an HTTP Request body to forward failures to an error-reporting service.
A second, `Filter`ed instance beside a specific feature, handling that area's errors without stopping the app-wide one from logging them.
antiPatterns: Matching on `Message` — it is free to be reworded between releases; match on `Code`.
Expecting one instance to consume an error so another does not see it; every instance whose Filter matches fires.
Using it in place of a node's own `Failure` output when the error is expected and the graph should branch on it where it happens.

ssr.note: File dialogs only exist in the browser.

enrichment.summary: Opens the browser's native file dialog on a signal and outputs the picked file plus its name, size and MIME type.
enrichment.description: When the `open` (Open) signal fires, the node clicks a hidden HTML file input, showing the browser's native file dialog. When the user picks a file, the `file` output delivers the browser File object (the value upload nodes expect), the Metadata outputs update, and `success` fires. If the user cancels the dialog, nothing fires — there is no cancel event. The selection is reset after each pick, so choosing the same file again still triggers `success`. `acceptedFileTypes` maps to the file input's accept attribute; `capture` maps to the capture attribute, which on mobile devices requests a camera or microphone as the source.
enrichment.whenToUse: Use it whenever the user must supply a file from their device — avatar upload, CSV import — typically firing `open` from a Button's `onClick` and passing `file` to an Upload File node. It is browser-only; there is no folder or multi-file selection.

ports.open: Signal; opens the file dialog. Must come from a user-initiated signal such as a click — browsers block programmatic file dialogs outside user gestures.
ports.acceptedFileTypes: String value; the accept attribute, e.g. 'image/*' or '.png,.csv'. Filters the dialog but is not validation — verify `type` if it matters.
ports.capture: String value; the capture attribute ('user' or 'environment'). On mobile, requests capturing from the front or rear camera instead of browsing files.
ports.file: Untyped value; the picked browser File object — wire this to Upload File.
ports.name: String value; the picked file's filename.
ports.sizeInBytes: Number value; the picked file's size in bytes.
ports.type: String value; the picked file's MIME type, e.g. 'image/png'.
ports.path: String value; read from the File object's path property, which standard browsers do not provide — usually undefined. Use `name` instead.
ports.success: Signal; fires after a file has been picked and all outputs are updated. Never fires on cancel.

patterns: Button `onClick` → `open`, then `file` → Upload File and `success` → the upload's trigger: the standard upload flow.
Latch `success` into a Boolean (value pinned true, `success` → Set) to reveal post-pick UI as a level.
antiPatterns: Treating `acceptedFileTypes` as a guarantee — users can often override the filter; check `type`/`sizeInBytes` before acting on the file.

enrichment.summary: Logical OR over any number of boolean inputs: Result is true while at least one connected input is true.
enrichment.description: Or combines an unbounded series of boolean inputs into one boolean `result` (Result) value output, which is true while any input is truthy. Inputs are coerced with plain JavaScript truthiness, so an input that has never received a value counts as false, and with nothing connected the result is false. Whenever any input changes, the result is recomputed and pushed downstream. It is a pure value node with no signals and no state of its own.
enrichment.whenToUse: Use it when any one of several conditions should be enough — e.g. show a section if either of two checkboxes is ticked. For 'all of' semantics use And; for negating one boolean use Inverter; for conditions that need comparisons or arithmetic first, compute them in an Expression and combine here.

ports.result: Boolean value; true while at least one connected input is true. With no inputs connected it is false.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: Inputs are numbered ports named "input 0", "input 1", … counting from 0 (displayed as "Input 0", "Input 1"). An authoring tool should connect booleans to "input N" names, using consecutive indices starting at 0.
patterns: Several error booleans → "input 0", "input 1", … with `result` → an error banner's `visible`: show it while anything is wrong.
`result` → Inverter → `enabled`: disable an action while any blocker is active.

enrichment.summary: The root visual node of a Router page component: declares the page's title, URL pattern and meta tags.
enrichment.description: Page is the mandatory root of every page component shown by a Router (Page Router) — a Router only mounts components whose graph contains exactly one Page node. It is not in the node picker because the editor creates it automatically when a page is added to a Router; there is no replacement node, you configure the existing one. Its `title` sets the document title and the Router's `currentPageTitle`; its `urlPath` is the page's URL pattern and may contain `{param}` placeholders that Page Inputs (PageInputs) nodes read; the remaining inputs are SEO meta tags (description, robots, og:*, twitter:*, sitemap hints) plus padding and CSS styling for the page surface.
enrichment.whenToUse: Do not add Page from the node picker or use it outside a Router page component — it is created automatically as the root when a page is added to a Router. Edit that existing node to set the page's title, `urlPath` and meta tags.

ports.title: String value; the page title, shown as the document title when the page is active. Defaults to the component name.
ports.urlPath: String value; the URL pattern that routes to this page, e.g. "product/{productId}" — placeholders become path parameters readable via PageInputs. Defaults to the title, lowercased and hyphenated.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: Runtime-determined inputs (runtime-discovered): `title` and `urlPath` are registered per instance by the editor connection, with defaults derived from the component name. The static catalog lists only the meta-tag, sitemap and padding inputs.

enrichment.summary: Component Stack: push/pop navigation container — pages stack on top of each other with transitions, ideal for wizards and drill-in flows.
enrichment.description: The Component Stack is the second navigation model, alongside Router. It holds a configured set of pages (components) and shows one at a time, but keeps history as a stack: Push Component To Stack adds a page on top (with a transition), Pop Component Stack returns to the one beneath, optionally handing back result values. `stackDepth` and `topPageName` expose the current state; `reset` unwinds to the start page. Unlike Router it is not URL-driven by default (`useRoutes` opts pages into routing).
enrichment.whenToUse: Flows with a natural back relationship: wizards, mobile-style master→detail drill-ins, modal sequences that return results. For top-level app sections addressed by URL, use Router + Page.

ports.pages: The stack's page components and the start page (editor-configured).
ports.reset: Signal; unwinds the stack to its start page.
ports.topPageName: String level naming the currently visible page.
ports.stackDepth: Number level; 1 means at the root, >1 means back is meaningful.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: Runtime-determined ports follow the configured pages: page components' inputs surface where relevant, and the pages list itself is a proplist the editor manages. Navigation nodes reference the stack by its `name`.
patterns: `stackDepth` → an Expression (`depth > 1`) → the back button's `visible`: back affordance only when back exists.
antiPatterns: Using a stack for top-level sections users expect to deep-link — that is Router territory.

dynamicPorts.description: Output ports are the path/query parameters declared on the containing page component (PageInputsAdapter).

parameterEncoding.reason: Ports are computed by the editor from the route that reaches the containing page component (PageInputsAdapter).

enrichment.summary: Page Inputs: exposes the URL path and query parameters of the containing page as value outputs.
enrichment.description: Page Inputs receives the navigation parameters delivered to the page component it sits in and republishes them as value outputs. Declare the expected names in the edit-only `pathParams` and `queryParams` string lists; each declared name becomes an output `pm-<name>` holding the value parsed from the URL (path placeholders like `{productId}` on the page's `urlPath`, or query-string entries) or passed by the Navigate node that opened the page. The Router pushes new values into these outputs on every navigation, including when only the parameters change while the page stays mounted.
enrichment.whenToUse: Inside a Router page component, whenever the page needs data that lives in the URL — a record id, a tab name, a search term. It only receives values pushed by the navigation system, so it does nothing outside a page component; for values passed to ordinary component instances use Component Inputs.

ports.pathParams: Edit-only string list; the path-parameter names to expose. Each name `x` becomes a `pm-x` value output.
ports.queryParams: Edit-only string list; the query-parameter names to expose, also surfaced as `pm-<name>` outputs.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: All outputs are runtime-determined (runtime-discovered + editor-adapter, PageInputsAdapter): declaring a name in `pathParams`/`queryParams` registers an untyped `pm-<name>` output on demand. The values themselves arrive when the Router (or a route-enabled Component Stack) navigates to the containing page and calls into this node; a generator can only rely on the names it declared itself.
patterns: `pm-<id>` → a Query Records filter input: the canonical detail page, where the record to show is chosen by the URL.
antiPatterns: Using Page Inputs to receive values from a normal component instance — that is what Component Inputs is for; Page Inputs is only fed by navigation.

enrichment.summary: Push Component To Stack: pushes a chosen page onto a named Component Stack with a transition when triggered.
enrichment.description: When `navigate` fires, the page selected on this node is pushed onto the Component Stack named in `stack`, animating per the chosen transition. Inputs declared by the target page's Component Inputs appear on this node, so per-page data travels with the push. `navigated` fires when the transition completes; `mode` controls push-vs-replace behaviour.
enrichment.whenToUse: Advancing stack flows: next wizard step, opening a detail page over a list. To go back, use Pop Component Stack — never push the previous page again.

ports.stack: Name of the target Component Stack (its `name` parameter).
ports.navigated: Signal; fires after the page transition finishes.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: The target-page choice, its transition options, and one input port per Component Input of the chosen page are runtime-determined from project content.
patterns: List row click → push detail page with the row's id wired into the page's input.

parameterEncoding.notes: Names are interpolated verbatim, including spaces — a value called `bg color` produces a port called `value-true-bg color`, not `value-true-bgColor`.

enrichment.summary: Pop Component Stack: returns to the previous page on the stack, optionally handing result values back to the popper's caller.
enrichment.description: When `navigate` fires, the top page is popped and the one beneath becomes visible with the reverse transition. The `results` list declares named values to pass back: they become inputs on this node, and the corresponding Push node that opened the page exposes them as outputs plus one signal per `backActions` entry — a lightweight way for a pushed page to answer the page that opened it.
enrichment.whenToUse: The back/cancel/done affordance inside any pushed page. Pair result values with distinct back actions ('save' vs 'cancel') when the opener must react differently.

ports.backActions: Named back reasons; each appears as a signal output on the corresponding push node.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: The result-value inputs are generated from the `results`/`backActions` lists on the node instance — runtime-determined by configuration.

enrichment.summary: Navigate To Path: jumps to an arbitrary URL path within the app, driving whichever routers match the path.
enrichment.description: Navigate To Path performs URL-level navigation: when `navigate` fires, the app's location changes to `path`, and the Router hierarchy resolves it exactly as if the user had typed the URL — including nested routers and page parameters embedded in the path. `queryNames` declares query-string values to attach; each name becomes an input. `openInNewTab` opens the path in a new tab instead.
enrichment.whenToUse: Cross-cutting jumps where composing router+page choices is clumsier than stating the destination path ('/projects/123/settings'), deep links, and programmatic redirects. enrichment.summary: REST node: a scripted request/response pair — request script shapes the call, response script maps the payload onto output ports.
enrichment.description: The REST node wraps one HTTP endpoint in two small scripts. The request script assembles method, resource and body from the node's script-declared `Inputs`; the response script reads `Response.content`/`Response.status` and assigns `Outputs`, and those script-declared names are the node's ports. `fetch` runs the request, `success`/`failure` report the outcome, `cancel` aborts in flight.
enrichment.whenToUse: Recurring API endpoints that deserve a typed port surface — the mapping lives in the node, the graph sees clean ports. For a quick GET with no mapping, HTTP Request is lighter; for secrets or server-side work, call a cloud function instead of embedding keys client-side.

ports.resource: The URL (the request script may parameterise it from inputs).
ports.requestScript: Script declaring inputs and shaping the outgoing request.
ports.responseScript: Script mapping the response onto declared outputs.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: All data ports are runtime-discovered from the two scripts' Inputs./Outputs. references, exactly like a Function node — write the scripts first, then wire to the names they declare.
antiPatterns: Embedding API secrets in the request script — anything client-side ships to the browser; put secrets behind a cloud function.

enrichment.summary: Page Router: a visual region that shows one page component at a time, driven by the browser URL and Navigate nodes.
enrichment.description: Router (Page Router) renders exactly one of its configured page components inside its own bounds. Its `pages` parameter is `{ routes: [component names], startPage: component name }`; each page component is rooted by a Page node whose `urlPath` defines the page's URL pattern, which may contain `{param}` placeholders. On mount the Router matches the current browser URL (hash-based by default, or real paths depending on the project's `navigationPathType` setting) and shows the matching page, falling back to `startPage`; a RouterNavigate node or a URL change switches pages, updates the browser URL and the document title, and delivers path/query parameters to Page Inputs (PageInputs) nodes inside the mounted page. Several Routers can coexist if given different `name`s; Navigate nodes address a router by that name (default "Main").
enrichment.whenToUse: The standard top-level navigation of an app: distinct pages with URLs, deep-linkable and back-button friendly. For push/pop sub-flows with transitions (wizards, drill-in) use Page Stack instead; a Router can nest inside another Router's page via its `urlPath` base-path input.

ports.name: String value identifying this router; RouterNavigate nodes target it by this name. Unset is treated as "Main".
ports.pages: Edit-only parameter `{ routes, startPage }` listing the page components this router can show. The URL pattern of each page comes from that page's own Page node, not from here.
ports.urlPath: String value prepended as a base path to every page's URL — used when this router is nested inside another router's page.
ports.reset: Signal input; re-evaluates the URL and rebuilds the current page (also updates Page Inputs if only params changed).
ports.currentPageTitle: String value; the title of the page currently shown (also written to the document title).
ports.currentPageComponent: String value; the component name of the page currently shown.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: Runtime-determined ports (runtime-discovered + editor-adapter, RouterAdapter): the `pages` parameter decides which page components exist, and the editor derives navigation metadata — page titles, URL patterns, parameters — from each page component's Page node. An authoring tool should set `name` and `pages` on the Router and declare titles/paths on the Page node inside each page component; it cannot enumerate page-dependent ports statically.
patterns: One Router named "Main" at the app root, with RouterNavigate nodes anywhere in the app switching it by name.
Declare `urlPath` with `{param}` placeholders on a page's Page node, then read the values with a Page Inputs node inside that page.
antiPatterns: Adding a Router per app section when one Router plus pages suffices — multiple routers are for genuinely independent regions (e.g. a main area and a side panel).

dynamicPorts.description: Ports are derived from the target router and the path parameters of the selected page component (RouterNavigateAdapter).

parameterEncoding.reason: Ports are computed by the editor from the target page component's parameters (RouterNavigateAdapter).

enrichment.summary: Navigate: tells a named Router to switch to a target page, passing typed path parameters, when its navigate signal fires.
enrichment.description: Navigate drives a Router. When `navigate` is triggered it switches the router named in its `router` parameter to the page chosen in `target`, updating the URL if the router does. Path/query parameters declared by the target page become input ports on this node, so per-page data (an id, a tab name) is wired like any other value. `navigated` fires when the transition completes; `openInNewTab` opens the target in a new browser tab instead of transitioning in place.
enrichment.whenToUse: All URL-style page switching with a Router. For stack-style flows (push/pop with transitions, e.g. wizards or mobile-style drill-in) use Page Stack with PageStackNavigate instead; for external URLs use net.noodl.externallink.

ports.navigate: Signal; performs the navigation. Typically fed from a Button's `onClick`.
ports.navigated: Signal; fires after the router has switched — sequence follow-up actions here.
ports.openInNewTab: Boolean; when true the navigation opens a new tab rather than switching this router.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: Runtime-determined inputs (runtime-discovered + editor-adapter): the `router` and `target` choices come from the routers and pages that exist in the project, and each parameter declared by the chosen target page is registered as an input port on demand. The port set therefore depends on project content, not the node type.
patterns: Button `onClick` → `navigate` with `target` set on the node: the standard menu/link wiring.
Record id from a list item → the page-parameter input, so the detail page can query its record from the URL.
antiPatterns: Encoding app state in many routers when one router plus page parameters suffices; multiple routers are for genuinely independent regions.

enrichment.summary: Run Tasks: executes a worker component once per array element with bounded concurrency, firing done/failure when the batch completes.
enrichment.description: Run Tasks is batch processing without visuals: for each element of `items` it instantiates `taskTemplate` (a component, not rendered), feeds the element's properties to the worker's Component Inputs, and waits for the worker to signal success or failure through its Component Outputs before scheduling the next, keeping at most `maxRunningTasks` in flight. `done` fires when every task finished; `stopOnFailure` aborts the rest after the first failure, and `abort` cancels mid-batch.
enrichment.whenToUse: Sequenced bulk work: importing rows, uploading a list of files, migrating records. For rendering a list use the Repeater; for one async action a Function node suffices.

ports.run: Signal; starts the batch over the current `items`.
ports.taskTemplate: The worker component; it must expose success/failure signal Component Outputs for scheduling to advance.
ports.maxRunningTasks: Concurrency ceiling; 1 gives strict sequential processing.
ports.done: Signal; the whole batch finished (respecting stopOnFailure).

patterns: Build the batch with New Array/Array, then `created` → `run`: data assembly and execution stay separate.
antiPatterns: Using a Repeater with invisible items as a work queue — Run Tasks exists precisely so batch work needs no render tree.

ssr.note: The viewport size is unknowable server-side; width/height stay unset until the browser runs.

enrichment.summary: Outputs the browser viewport's width, height and aspect ratio, updating live on every window resize.
enrichment.description: Screen Resolution reports the size of the browser viewport — despite the name it reads window.innerWidth/innerHeight, not the physical screen. `width` and `height` are levels in CSS pixels, `aspectRatio` is width divided by height, and all three update automatically whenever the window resizes (including device rotation). The node has no inputs.
enrichment.whenToUse: Use it to drive responsive logic in the graph: feed `width` into an Expression or Condition to produce breakpoint booleans ('narrow layout?') that control visibility or layout inputs. For purely visual responsiveness, prefer the built-in sizing/variants of visual nodes; reach for this node when logic must know the viewport size.

ports.width: Number level; current viewport width in CSS pixels (window.innerWidth), updated on resize.
ports.height: Number level; current viewport height in CSS pixels (window.innerHeight), updated on resize.
ports.aspectRatio: Number level; width / height — greater than 1 in landscape, less than 1 in portrait.

patterns: `width` → Expression `width < 600` → a Group's or Text's `visible`: show compact-layout elements only on narrow viewports.

parameterEncoding.reason: The `name` parameter selects which variable is written; it does not appear in any port name. The single dynamic port is `value`, whose *type* follows the `setWith` parameter.

enrichment.summary: Writes one named app-wide variable when its Do signal fires, converting the value per the 'Set as' type choice.
enrichment.description: Set Variable stores a value into the named app-wide variable — the same store Variable2 reads — only when the `do` (Do) signal fires; the incoming value is held but nothing is written before that. `setWith` (Set as, parameters-only) selects the value type: it types the node's dynamic `value` input and controls conversion on store — 'boolean' coerces with !!, 'emptyString' writes '' and removes the value input entirely, and 'object'/'array' accept a shared Object/Array id string and resolve it to the actual object or collection before storing. Writes always use force-change semantics, so Variable2 nodes bound to that name fire `changed` even when the new value equals the old one. `done` fires after the store completes.
enrichment.whenToUse: Use it when writing shared state should happen at an explicit moment — on click, on submit, after a fetch — or when you need the type conversions ('Set as'). For continuous write-on-change semantics, wire into a Variable2 node's `value` input instead; to clear a variable, choose Set as 'Empty string'.

ports.do: Signal; performs the store, then fires `done`. Nothing is written until this fires.
ports.name: String value input naming the variable to write; shares the same namespace as Variable2.
ports.setWith: Editor-only enum ('Set as'); selects the dynamic value input's type and the conversion applied when storing. Cannot be connected.
ports.done: Signal; fires after the value has been stored.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: The value input is runtime-determined: the editor pushes a single dynamic input port named `value` whose type follows the `setWith` parameter ('*' when unset), and no value port exists at all when setWith is 'emptyString'. The runtime registers `value` on demand when a connection or parameter references it. An authoring tool may wire or set `value` (except in emptyString mode) and must set `setWith` via parameters, never a connection.
patterns: Button `onClick` → `do` with the form's data on `value`: commit shared state at the moment of a user action.
`done` → a navigation or feedback signal: sequence 'store, then move on' explicitly.
antiPatterns: Expecting the write to happen when `value` changes — Set Variable only writes on `do`. Use Variable2's value input for write-on-change.

enrichment.summary: Set Record Properties: writes property values to an existing cloud database record when Do is triggered.
enrichment.description: SetDbModelProperties (Set Record Properties) updates the record identified by `modelId` in the class chosen with the `collectionName` (Class) parameter. Each class property becomes a value input; triggering `store` (Do) applies the connected inputs to the local record and saves them to the server, firing `stored` (Success) on confirmation or `failure` with `error` on problems. `storeType` (Store to) can switch the node to 'Local only', which updates the in-memory record without any server call — useful for optimistic UI or scratch state. By default only the properties you actually supply are sent (`storeProperties` = 'Only specified'); 'All' sends the record's entire current data. Because the shared local record is updated, every bound Record node and live query in the app sees the change immediately.
enrichment.whenToUse: The save half of every edit form, and the way to flip a single field ('mark done') from a list row. To create a record use NewDbModelProperties; to remove one use DeleteDbModelProperties; for BYOB backends use noodl.byob.UpdateRecord.

ports.store: Signal (displayed as Do); saves to cloud (default) or applies locally, depending on `storeType`.
ports.stored: Signal (displayed as Success); fires after the server confirms the save (or immediately after a local-only store).
ports.modelId: Value input: id of the record to update (a record object is also accepted). Shown while `idSource` is 'Specify explicitly'.
ports.idSource: Edit-only choice: 'Specify explicitly' uses `modelId`; 'From repeater' targets the record driving the nearest enclosing For Each item.
ports.storeProperties: Edit-only choice ('Only specified' / 'All'): whether to send just the supplied property inputs or the record's whole data. Shown while `storeType` is cloud.
ports.storeType: Edit-only choice ('Cloud and local' / 'Local only'): whether the save reaches the server or only the in-memory record.
ports.accessControl: Edit-only list of access rules applied with the save; each rule expands into its own Target/Read/Write inputs.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: Ports are runtime-determined: `collectionName` (Class) is registered as an edit-only enum of the project's classes plus _User/_Role, and each schema property of the chosen class becomes a value input `prop-<name>` typed from the schema. Access Control rules spawn `acl-<ruleId>-*` inputs like on Create New Record. An authoring tool should set `collectionName` in parameters and drive the `prop-<name>` inputs it intends to change.
patterns: DbModel2 `prop-<name>` → Text Input `startValue`, edited `text` → `prop-<name>`, Button `onClick` → `store`: prefill, edit, save.
'From repeater' `idSource` inside a list row: one node updates whichever record the row represents.
antiPatterns: Setting `storeProperties` to 'All' to 'be safe' — it uploads the record's entire local data and can overwrite fields other users changed; send only what the form edits.

enrichment.summary: Set Object Properties: writes declared property values onto an existing client-side object, chosen by id or from the repeater item.
enrichment.description: Set Object Properties mutates an object in the client-side object store. The target is chosen by `idSource` (Id Source): with 'Specify explicitly' (the default) the `modelId` (Id) input names the object — it accepts either an id string or an object value directly; with 'From repeater' the node walks up the component tree and targets the item object of the closest enclosing Repeater (For Each) item, which is the idiomatic way to edit "this row's" data from inside an item component. When `store` (Do) fires, every property declared in `properties` is written from its input, then `stored` (Done) fires. Because everything bound to the same object shares it, the change immediately propagates to Object nodes, repeater item bindings and Component Inputs reading that object.
enrichment.whenToUse: Use it to change one or more properties of an existing client-side object in a single action — especially from inside a repeater item with Id Source 'From repeater'. To create the object first use Create New Object (NewModel); to write a single property continuously prefer an Object (Model2) node's property inputs; for cloud records use Set Record Properties (SetDbModelProperties) plus a save to persist.

ports.idSource: Edit-only enum choosing the target: 'explicit' uses `modelId`; 'foreach' uses the closest enclosing repeater item's object (the `modelId` input disappears in this mode).
ports.modelId: Value input naming the target object; accepts an id string or an object value (its id is used).
ports.store: Signal input; writes all declared property inputs to the target after pending input updates settle, then fires `stored`.
ports.stored: Signal; fires after the properties have been written. Does not fire if no target object is set.
ports.id: String value; the id of the current target object.
ports.properties: Edit-only stringlist declaring which property names this node writes; each becomes a `prop-<name>` input.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior:
Property inputs are runtime-discovered from the `properties` parameter: each declared name p produces a value input `prop-

` (group Property Values) and an edit-only enum `type-

` (String/Boolean/Number/Date/Array/Object/Any, default Any). Only names present in `properties` are written on store. Additionally a declared port group hides `modelId` unless `idSource` is 'explicit' (or unset). Static values can be supplied as `prop-

` parameters instead of connections.
patterns: Inside a repeater item component: `idSource` = 'foreach', a button's click → `store`: edit the current row's object without passing ids around.
Create New Object `id` → `modelId`: set further properties on a just-created object.
antiPatterns: Using it on cloud record objects and expecting the database to change — writes are client-side only; follow with a Save Record action to persist.

enrichment.summary: Mints a short-lived signed URL for a cloud file, for previewing or downloading files uploaded as private.
enrichment.description: Sign File URL takes a `cloudfile` handle (from Upload File or a record's file property) and, when `sign` fires, asks the backend for a time-limited signed URL to it. A private file's plain `url` 403s for anyone but its owner; the signed URL works for the short window it is valid, which is the intended usage — sign right before rendering, not once and persist. On `success` the signed `url`, its `expiresAt`, and `ttlSeconds` are available; `failure` carries `error`/`errorStatus` the same shape Upload File uses.
enrichment.whenToUse: Previewing or linking to a file that was uploaded with Upload File's `private` input set. Not needed for public (non-private) files — their plain `cloudFile.url` already works for anyone who can reach the app.

ports.file: The cloudfile to sign; set before firing `sign`.
ports.sign: Signal; requests a fresh signed URL. Re-fire before every use — a previously signed URL expires.
ports.url: The signed URL, valid until `expiresAt`/for `ttlSeconds` seconds from when `sign` fired.
ports.expiresAt: ISO timestamp the signed URL stops working.
ports.ttlSeconds: How long the signed URL is valid for, in seconds, from when it was minted.

patterns: Fire `sign` from the same signal that produced the `cloudFile` (e.g. Upload File's `success`), so the graph never holds a `cloudFile` without also having signed it.
antiPatterns: Persisting a signed `url` (e.g. saving it to a record) instead of the plain cloudfile — the signature expires and the stored link stops working; store the cloudfile, sign again at render time.

parameterEncoding.notes: Names are interpolated verbatim, including spaces — a value called `bg color` produces a port called `value-true-bg color`, not `value-true-bgColor`.

enrichment.summary: Named state machine: define states and values, set each value per state, and outputs switch or tween when the state changes.
enrichment.description: States is configured with two editable lists: `states` (state names, e.g. 'Hidden,Shown') and `values` (value names, e.g. 'opacity,tint'). From these the editor generates ports: each value becomes an output whose current setting depends on the active state, and each state gets ports to enter it and observe it. On a state change every value output updates — number and color values tween along per-state transition curves (default 300 ms ease-out bezier), while string, boolean and textStyle values switch instantly. The first state in the list is the initial state; it is applied at startup without firing `stateChanged`. This is the idiomatic node for coordinated show/hide and multi-property animations.
enrichment.whenToUse: Reach for States whenever several properties must change together between named modes (open/closed, idle/loading/done) — it replaces the deprecated Animation and Transition nodes. For animating a single number toward a moving target use net.noodl.animatetovalue; for pure branching logic with no animated values use Condition or Switch.

ports.states: Comma-separated state names (parameter only, not connectable). The first name is the initial state.
ports.values: Comma-separated value names (parameter only); each name becomes a value output plus one input per state.
ports.toggle: Signal; advances to the next state in list order, wrapping around — a one-connection two-state toggle.
ports.useTransitions: Boolean; when false every state change is instant and the per-state transition curve inputs are removed.
ports.currentState: String output with the active state's name; it updates at the start of a transition, not when the tween finishes.
ports.stateChanged: Signal; fires on every state change except the initial state applied at startup.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: All state- and value-specific ports are runtime-discovered: the viewer generates them from the `states` and `values` parameters and pushes them to the editor per instance. For each value V: an output named `V` (connections only; type chosen by a generated enum input `type-V` — number, string, boolean, color or textStyle, default number). For each state S and value V: an input `value-S-V` holding V's setting while in state S. For each state S: a signal input `to-S` (go to S), a boolean output `at-S` (true while S is active), a signal output `reached-S` (fires when the transition into S completes — immediately when there is no transition), and, while `useTransitions` is on, a curve input `transitiondef-S` (state-wide default) plus per-value overrides `transition-S-V` for number/color values. A generated enum input `currentState` sets the state by name. An authoring tool should write `states`, `values`, `type-V` and `value-S-V` as parameters, wire signals to `to-S`, and read `V`, `at-S` and `reached-S` — the runtime registers these names on demand.
patterns: Button `onClick` → `to-<state>` to enter a specific state; `toggle` when there are exactly two states.
One value output → a Group's `opacity` and another → Color Blend `blendValue`: several properties animate together from a single state change.
`at-<state>` (boolean) → `visible` or `enabled` inputs: gate UI on the current state as a level.
`reached-<state>` (signal) → a follow-up action: sequence work after the transition finishes ( `stateChanged` fires at the start, `reached-` at the end).
antiPatterns: Comparing `currentState` strings in an Expression to derive booleans — the generated `at-<state>` outputs already provide them.
Wiring `stateChanged` where 'animation done' is meant; it fires when the change starts. Use `reached-<state>`.

enrichment.summary: Static Array: inline JSON or CSV authored in the editor, emitted as an array of objects.
enrichment.description: Static Array turns literal data typed into the node — JSON (an array of objects) or CSV with a header row — into an `items` array plus a `count`. Each element becomes a client-side object, so downstream nodes treat the items exactly like query results or shared-array elements.
enrichment.whenToUse: Fixtures, menus, option lists, demo content — any list that ships with the app rather than coming from a backend or user input. For runtime-mutable lists feed an Array (Collection2); for remote data use Query Records or REST.

ports.type: Chooses the authoring format: 'json' or 'csv'; the matching text input (`json`/`csv`) is shown.
ports.items: The parsed array; wire to a Repeater's `items` or into filters/maps.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: Declared-port-groups only: the `json` and `csv` text inputs swap in based on `type`. No ports depend on the data itself.
patterns: Static Array → Array Filter/Array Map → Repeater: fixture-driven UI with real list plumbing.
antiPatterns: Editing Static Array content from logic at runtime — it is authoring-time data; use an Array for mutable lists.

inputs.name: treatEmptyAs
inputs.description: Back-compat for graphs written before Variables were nullable. `null` (default) keeps a cleared value distinguishable from a real "". Choosing another option restores the pre-NDA-003 coercion for authors who relied on it.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The empty-value contract (dev-docs/reference/EMPTY-VALUE-CONTRACT.md): `undefined` abstains and leaves the Variable's stored value untouched. `null` is a real value — it clears the Variable, is stored, and fires Changed. What "cleared" is stored as is controlled by `Treat empty as` (null by default).

outputs.name: length
outputs.description: 0 when the Variable is cleared (`savedValue` is `null`) — there is no text to measure, and 0 is what an author reading this as a plain number expects, rather than a thrown error or `null` itself.

outputs.name: savedValue
outputs.description: Can be `null` — a cleared Variable (see `value`'s description) stores and emits null by default, not this type's zero value, unless `Treat empty as` says otherwise.

enrichment.summary: Per-instance text holder: stores one string locally, with a Length output and optional latch-until-Set behaviour.
enrichment.description: String holds a single text value that belongs to this node instance alone — it is not named or shared (for an app-wide named value use Variable2). The `value` input sets it and `savedValue` (Value) reads it back; `length` always reports the stored string's character count. While the `saveValue` (Set) signal input is unconnected, values written to `value` apply immediately; once `saveValue` is connected the node latches: incoming values are held pending and only applied when Set fires — the idiomatic way to snapshot a text field at the moment of a click. Incoming values are cast with JavaScript String(). `changed` fires only when the stored value actually changes; `stored` fires after every Set trigger.
enrichment.whenToUse: Use it to hold or snapshot local text: capture a Text Input's current value on submit, keep a reusable literal in one editable place, or derive `length` for validation. For text shared across components use Variable2 + Set Variable; for computed text use an Expression.

ports.value: String value input. Applies immediately when `saveValue` is unconnected; otherwise held until Set fires.
ports.saveValue: Signal; applies the most recently received `value`, then fires `stored`. Connecting it switches the node from pass-through to snapshot mode.
ports.savedValue: String level with the currently stored text.
ports.length: Number level; character count of the stored string, updated whenever the stored value changes.
ports.changed: Signal; fires only when the stored value actually changes.
ports.stored: Signal; fires after every Set trigger, even when the value did not change.

patterns: Snapshot on submit: Text Input `onTextChanged` → `value`, Button `onClick` → `saveValue`; `stored` then triggers whatever consumes the committed text.
`length` → an Expression or Condition for 'minimum characters' style validation.
antiPatterns: Using String nodes in two components to 'share' text — each instance has its own value. Use Variable2 for shared text.

outputs.name: formatted

enrichment.summary: Builds a string from a template: each {tag} in the Format text becomes an input port whose value is spliced in.
enrichment.description: String Format takes a template on its `format` (Format) parameter and outputs the filled-in text on `formatted` (Formatted), a string value. Every {tag} in the template (tag characters: letters, digits, underscore) becomes a string input port named exactly like the tag, and each occurrence is replaced by that input's current value — or by nothing while the input is still undefined. The same tag may appear multiple times; every occurrence is filled. The output recomputes after any input or the template changes, once per update cycle. The node displays its format text as its label in the editor.
enrichment.whenToUse: The idiomatic way to put values inside text: 'Saved at {time}', '{count} items', building URLs or messages from parts. For two fixed alternatives use Boolean To String; for value-keyed lookup use String Mapper; for transformations of the values themselves (padding, casing, math) do that upstream in an Expression or Function.

ports.format: String parameter with {tag} placeholders; changing it re-registers the input ports and reformats.
ports.formatted: String value output: the template with every {tag} replaced by its input's value (empty where an input is still undefined).

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: Input ports are created from the `format` parameter: each unique {tag} yields one string input named exactly <tag> (no braces). The editor updates the port list live as the format is edited. An authoring tool must first set `format`, then may connect to or set parameters for each tag name it wrote; no other inputs exist.
patterns: Counter `currentCount` → the {n} input of format "{n} pcs" → a Text's `text`: numbers cast to string on connection, so no converter node is needed.
antiPatterns: Tags with spaces or dashes ({item-count}) — tag names are limited to [A-Za-z0-9_]; anything else stays literal text.

enrichment.summary: Looks a string up in a configured key list and outputs the matching mapping — a wirable lookup table with a default.
enrichment.description: String Mapper compares `inputString` (Input String) against its numbered "input N" entries (displayed Input 0, Input 1, …) using exact string equality. On a match, the `mappedString` (Mapped String) output takes the value of the "output N" entry with the same N (displayed Mapping 0, Mapping 1, … — these mappings are themselves inputs, despite the port name); with no match it takes `defaultMapping` (Default). All values are coerced to strings before comparison, and the mapping re-runs once per update cycle after any of its inputs change. Keys and mappings are usually typed in as parameters but can also be connected.
enrichment.whenToUse: Use it to translate machine values into display text: status codes to labels, option keys to descriptions, locale keys to phrases. For just true/false use Boolean To String; for composing text with variables inside use String Format; for mappings that live in data rather than in the graph, use an Object or a Function.

ports.inputString: String value to look up; compared with strict equality after toString coercion.
ports.defaultMapping: String value used whenever no key matches — also the output before `inputString` first matches anything.
ports.mappedString: String value output: the mapping paired with the matched key, or `defaultMapping`.

enrichment.runtimeBehavior: Two numbered port series, both inputs, indexed from 0: keys are named "input 0", "input 1", … (group Inputs) and their mapped values are named "output 0", "output 1", … (group Mappings) — pair N maps key N to value N. The editor always offers the next unused index. An authoring tool typically writes both series as parameters (e.g. "input 0": "S", "output 0": "Small"), and may connect any of them.
patterns: A Radio Button Group's `value` → `inputString`, mappings to human copy → a Text's `text`: option keys stay short and stable while the UI text stays editable in one place.
antiPatterns: Using it for numeric ranges ('0-9' → 'low') — matching is exact equality only; use Expression or Condition chains for ranges.

inputs.name: start
inputs.description: Position of the first character to keep, counting from zero; a negative value counts back from the end

inputs.name: string
inputs.description: Text to take the substring from; it must not be cleared to null, which raises an error rather than yielding an empty result

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: The section of String between Start and End

enrichment.summary: Extracts part of a string between a start index (inclusive) and end index (exclusive).
enrichment.description: Substring takes a `string` (String) input and outputs the characters from index `start` (Start, 0-based, inclusive) up to but not including index `end` (End) on the `result` (Result) string value output. While `end` has never been set, the substring runs from `start` to the end of the string — so a node with only `start` configured behaves like 'drop the first N characters'. Setting `end` to -1 also means 'to the end of the string'. Non-string inputs are converted with toString() first, and any input change updates the result immediately.
enrichment.whenToUse: Use it for simple positional trims: a short prefix of an id, truncating a preview, slicing fixed-width data. For pattern-based extraction, case changes or search-and-replace, use Expression or a Function; for assembling text from parts, use String Format.

ports.end: Number value, exclusive end index. Left unset (or set to -1) the substring extends to the end of the string; note that an explicit 0 means an empty result, not 'to the end'.
ports.result: String value with the extracted range.

patterns: Unique Id `guid` → `string` with `start` 0 / `end` 4: a short human-readable tag from a longer id.
antiPatterns: Setting `end` to 0 expecting 'until the end' — 0 is a real exclusive index and yields an empty string; leave `end` unset or use -1 instead.

enrichment.summary: A remembered on/off boolean, driven by On / Off / Flip signals — the graph's toggle and one-bit memory.
enrichment.description: Switch stores a single boolean state. The `on` (On), `off` (Off) and `flip` (Flip) signal inputs change it; `onFromStart` (State) is a boolean value input that sets the state directly and provides its initial value (default false). The current state is always readable on the `state` (Current State) boolean value output, and every state change also fires signals: `switched` (Switched) on any change, plus `switchedToOn` or `switchedToOff` matching the new state. `on` and `off` are ignored when the state already matches, so they never re-fire the signals; `flip` always changes state.
enrichment.whenToUse: The idiomatic node for anything a user toggles: expand/collapse, mute, edit mode. Use `state` (a level) to drive `visible`/`enabled`-style inputs, and the switched signals only when something must happen at the moment of change. For more than two states use States; for deriving a boolean from data rather than events, use Condition or Expression.

ports.flip: Signal; inverts the state and always fires the switched signals.
ports.on: Signal; sets the state to true. Does nothing (and fires nothing) if it is already true.
ports.off: Signal; sets the state to false. Does nothing (and fires nothing) if it is already false.
ports.onFromStart: Boolean value (displayed as State); sets the state directly and defines the initial state. Changing it also fires the switched signals.
ports.state: Boolean value that always reflects the current state — wire this to `visible`/`enabled` style inputs.
ports.switched: Signal; fires on every state change, after `state` has been updated.
ports.switchedToOn: Signal; fires when a change leaves the state true.
ports.switchedToOff: Signal; fires when a change leaves the state false.

patterns: Button `onClick` → `flip`, `state` → a Group's `visible`: the standard show/hide toggle.
`state` → Boolean To String `input` → the toggling button's `label`: the button describes what it will do next.
antiPatterns: Wiring `switchedToOn` (a momentary signal) to a boolean input like `visible` — it delivers only a pulse; use `state` for anything that must stay on.

Typography comes either from a project-wide `textStyle` (preferred, keeps the app consistent) or from explicit `fontFamily`/`fontSize`/`color` parameters that override it. ssr.note: The scheduler clock is frozen during server render, so Started/Finished never fire there; do not gate Page Ready on a Delay.

enrichment.summary: Delay: fires a Finished signal a set number of milliseconds after being started; restartable for debouncing.
enrichment.description: Timer (displayed as Delay) turns one signal into a later signal. Triggering `start` (Start) begins a countdown of `duration` milliseconds (after an optional `startDelay`, also milliseconds); when it completes, `timerFinished` (Finished) fires. `timerStarted` (Started) fires at the moment the countdown actually begins. `start` does nothing while the timer is already running, whereas `restart` (Restart) always begins the countdown again from zero — that difference is what makes `restart` the debounce input. `stop` (Stop) cancels a running countdown without firing `timerFinished`. With the default `duration` of 0 the finish fires on the next tick, which still defers the signal until after the current update.
enrichment.whenToUse: Use it to defer an action (auto-dismiss a toast, poll once after mount) or, via `restart`, to debounce a noisy source such as typing. For repeating ticks, loop `timerFinished` back into `restart`. For animating a value over time use Animation instead — Timer carries no value, only timing.

ports.start: Signal; starts the countdown only if the timer is not already running.
ports.restart: Signal; starts the countdown unconditionally, restarting from zero if already running — use for debouncing.
ports.stop: Signal; cancels the countdown; `timerFinished` will not fire.
ports.startDelay: Number value in milliseconds added before the countdown begins (default 0).
ports.timerStarted: Signal; fires when the countdown actually starts (also on each restart).
ports.timerFinished: Signal; fires once when the countdown completes; suppressed by `stop`.

patterns: Value Changed `valueChanged` → `restart`, act on `timerFinished`: debounce — the action runs only after the input has been quiet for `duration` ms.
`timerFinished` → its own `restart`: a simple repeating tick.
antiPatterns: Using `start` for debouncing — while running it ignores triggers, so the action fires on the first quiet gap after the *first* event, not the last. Use `restart`.
Treating `duration` as seconds — it is milliseconds.

ssr.note: The scheduler clock is frozen during server render; the transition does not animate or complete there.

One id is generated when the node initializes, so `guid` is usable immediately; triggering the `new` (New) signal input replaces it with a fresh id and pushes the change downstream. patterns: The signal that creates a local item also triggers `new`, and `guid` is stored with the item: every item gets its own key.

enrichment.summary: Uploads a browser file to cloud storage when triggered, reporting progress and yielding a cloudfile handle.
enrichment.description: Upload File takes a browser File (typically from Open File Picker) on its untyped `file` input and, when `upload` fires, stores it in the cloud backend's file storage. Progress streams out (`progressLoadedPercent`, byte counts, `progressChanged`), and on `success` the stored file is available as `cloudFile` — the handle to attach to a record's file property or unwrap with Cloud File. `failure` carries `error` and `errorStatus`.
enrichment.whenToUse: Attachments, avatars, imports — any user-picked file that must persist server-side. The upload stores the file only; associating it with a record is a separate write (Create/Set Record).

ports.file: The browser file to upload; untyped so any file source connects.
ports.private: Boolean, default false. When true the backend ACLs the upload to its uploader instead of leaving it public — the resulting cloudfile's plain `url` then only works for the uploader (or an admin); use Sign File URL to get a usable link back out.
ports.cloudFile: The stored file's handle, valid from `success` onward.
ports.progressLoadedPercent: Number level 0–100 while uploading; drive progress UI from here.

patterns: Picker `success` → `upload`, upload `success` → record write: three nodes, each owning one step.
`private: true` uploads pair with Sign File URL: wire the same `success` signal to both the record write and the signer.
antiPatterns: Treating `cloudFile` as set before `success` fired — sequence record writes on the success signal.
Setting `private: true` and then binding `cloudFile.url` straight to an Image/link — a private file's plain url 403s for anyone but the uploader; sign it first.

enrichment.summary: Turns value changes into events: fires a signal every time its input receives a different value.
enrichment.description: Value Changed watches one input of any type (`value`, displayed as Input) and fires the `valueChanged` (Value Changed) signal each time the incoming value differs from the last one it saw — including the very first value it receives. Comparison uses strict equality, so for objects and arrays a change means a different reference, not a mutation of the same object. It is the bridge from the value world (levels) to the signal world (events).
enrichment.whenToUse: Use it when something must happen at the moment data changes: restart a debounce Timer while the user types, re-run a Function when a selection changes, or trigger a save when a field updates. If you only need the value itself downstream, connect the value directly — no node needed. If you care about a boolean becoming true specifically, connect the boolean straight to a signal input (rising-edge trigger) instead.

ports.value: Value input of any type; each strictly-unequal new value fires the output. Object/array mutations without a new reference do not count as changes.
ports.valueChanged: Signal; fires once per detected change, including the first value ever received.

patterns: A text input's `text` → `value`, `valueChanged` → a Timer's `restart`: debounce — the Timer only finishes once typing pauses.
`valueChanged` → an Event Sender's `sendEvent`: broadcast that a piece of state changed.
antiPatterns: Using it to detect a boolean turning true — it also fires on true→false. Connect the boolean directly to the target signal input (edge-triggered) or use Condition.

enrichment.summary: Deprecated first-generation named app-wide variable node; superseded by Variable2 and Set Variable.
enrichment.description: The original read/write node for the named app-wide variable store, with an explicit `store` (Set) signal to commit its `value` input. It is superseded by Variable2 (shown as 'Variable' in the picker), which writes whenever its value input receives data, together with Set Variable for explicit signal-driven writes with type control. Both read and write the same underlying store as this node.
enrichment.whenToUse: Do not use in new graphs — use Variable2 to read and write a named variable, and Set Variable for explicit signal-driven writes.

enrichment.summary: Reads and writes one named app-wide variable; every node bound to the same name sees the same value.
enrichment.description: Variable2 (shown as 'Variable' in the editor) binds to one entry in the app-wide variable store — a single shared, untyped key/value map for the running session (in memory only, not persisted across reloads). `name` selects the variable; the `value` output reads it, and the `value` *input* writes it: sending a value in stores it under the current name for every other Variable node to see. When the variable is written anywhere else in the app, `changed` fires and the `value` output updates automatically. Connecting the `fetch` signal input changes this to pull mode: external changes and name changes no longer propagate on their own, and the node only re-reads when `fetch` fires, after which `fetched` fires. This is the shared counterpart of the per-instance Boolean/Number/String/Color holders, which each keep a private value.
enrichment.whenToUse: Use it for state shared across components — the logged-in user's name, a selected id, a UI mode — reading it where needed and writing via its `value` input or, for explicit signal-driven writes with type control, a Set Variable node. For a value used only inside one component prefer a per-instance holder (Boolean/Number/String/Color); for structured data use Model2.

ports.name: String value input naming the variable; all Variable/Set Variable nodes with the same name share one value. With `fetch` unconnected, changing the name immediately re-reads and fires `fetched`.
ports.value: As an input: writes — the received value is stored into the named variable. As an output: the variable's current value (untyped).
ports.fetch: Signal; re-reads the named variable on demand. Connecting it disables automatic updates — external changes then reach the outputs only when Fetch fires.
ports.changed: Signal; fires when the variable is changed from anywhere in the app (suppressed while `fetch` is connected).
ports.fetched: Signal; fires after each read triggered by `fetch` or by a name change.

patterns: Set Variable writes on a user action; Variable2 nodes with the same name anywhere in the app update reactively — the idiomatic shared-state shape.
`value` output → an Expression → visual inputs: derive display text or booleans from shared state where it is consumed.
antiPatterns: Expecting each Variable2 instance to hold its own value — the name is the identity, all instances with one name share one value. For private per-node state use Boolean/Number/String/Color.
Using variables as persistent storage — the store is in-memory and resets on page reload; persist important data in the cloud database or browser storage nodes.

enrichment.summary: Plays video from a URL or MediaStream, with play/pause/restart/reset signals and playback-position output.
enrichment.description: Video renders an HTML `video` element. `src` (a string URL or project asset path) or `srcObject` (a MediaStream, e.g. a camera feed) supplies the media; `poster` shows an image before playback; `autoplay`, `loop`, `muted`, `controls` and `volume` map directly onto the element. Playback is driven by four signal inputs: `play` resumes, `pause` pauses, `restart` seeks to the start and plays, `reset` seeks to the start and pauses. Outputs report state: `onPlay`/`onPause`/`onCanPlay` are signals from the element's events, `onTimeUpdate` (Playback Position) is a number holding the current time in seconds, and `videoWidth`/`videoHeight` give the intrinsic size once known.
